RFA No. HHS0016125 Exhibit D ARTICLE 4. BREACH NOTICE, REPORTING AND CORRECTION REQUIREMENTS Section 4.01. Cooperation and Financial Responsibility. (A) Contractor shall, at Contractor’s expense, cooperate fully with HHS in investigating, mitigating to the extent practicable, and issuing notifications as directed by HHS, for any Breach of Confidential Information. (B) Contractor shall make Confidential Information in Contractor’s possession available pursuant to the requirements of HIPAA or other applicable law upon a determination of a Breach. (C) Contractor’s obligation begins at the Discovery of a Breach and continues as long as related activity continues, until all effects of the Breach are mitigated to HHS’s satisfaction (the "incident response period"). Section 4.02. Initial Breach Notice. For federal information obtained from a federal system of records , including Federal Tax Information and Social Security Administration Data (which includes Medicaid and other governmental benefit program Confidential Information), Contractor shall notify HHS of the Breach within the first consecutive clock hour of Discovery. The Base Contract shall specify whether Confidential Information is obtained from a federal system of records. For all other types of Confidential Information Contractor shall notify HHS of the Breach not more than 24 hours after Discovery, or in a timeframe otherwise approved by HHS in writing. Contractor shall initially report to HHS's Privacy and Security Officers via email at: privacy@HHSC.state.tx.us and to the HHS division responsible for the Base Contract. Contractor shall report all information reasonably available to Contractor about the Breach. Contractor shall provide contact information to HHS for Contractor's single point of contact who will communicate with HHS both on and off business hours during the incident response period. Section 4.03 Third Business Day Notice : No later than 5 p.m. on the third business day after Discovery, or a time within which Discovery reasonably should have been made by Contractor of a Breach of Confidential Information, Contractor shall provide written notification to HHS of all reasonably available information about the Breach, and Contractor's investigation, including, to the extent known to Contractor : a. The date the Breach occurred; b. The date of Contractor's and, if applicable, Subcontractor's Discovery; c. A brief description of the Breach, including how it occurred and who is responsible (or hypotheses, if not yet determined); d. A brief description of Contractor's investigation and the status of the investigation; e. A description of the types and amount of Confidential Information involved; f. Identification of and number of all individuals reasonably believed to be affected, including first and last name of the individual and if applicable, the Legally authorized representative, last known address, age, telephone number, and email address if it is a preferred contact method; g. Contractor’s initial risk assessment of the Breach demonstrating whether individual or other notices are required by applicable law or this DUA for HHS approval, including an analysis of whether there is a low probability of compromise of the Confidential Information or whether any legal exceptions to notification apply; h. Contractor's recommendation for HHS’s approval as to the steps individuals and/or Contractor on behalf of individuals, should take to protect the individuals from potential harm, including HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 7 of 11

data.title: TX - 2026 - Attachment A-1 Data Definitions
data.highlights: This supporting document defines key terms for eligibility, assessment, service participation, care models, and outcome tracking in the Texas RHTP Behavioral Health/Housing program. Definitions cover client types, program milestones, types of housing and support services, integrated healthcare, diversion from justice involvement, and workforce development for homeless individuals with behavioral health needs.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form I Thriving Texas Families Project Sites And Hours
data.highlights: This is a required form for applicants to list service sites and hours under the Thriving Texas Families program RFA. It collects information on site location, hours of operation, and service coverage for contract incorporation.

data.title: TX - 2005 - FORM D - Entity Information and Contract Litigation History
data.highlights:
Form D collects entity identification, nonprofit status, conflict of interest disclosures, prior contract and litigation history, and applicant relationships with the Texas Health and Human Services Commission. It ensures applicants meet eligibility, transparency, and compliance requirements for participation in the RHTP procurement.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Solicitation RFA HHS0016203 Exhibit J, Goals and Outcomes
data.highlights: This guidance document sets forth the expected goals, population health priorities, and outcome measures for RHTP-related applications, focusing on maternal health, child development, workforce readiness, and family stability. Activities emphasize connecting clients to a broad range of community, behavioral, health, educational, housing, and workforce resources. It details specific metrics for evaluating client engagement, resource referrals, and knowledge improvement.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form H, Internal Controls Questionnaire
data.highlights: Form H is a required internal controls questionnaire for applicants to the Texas RHTP program. It assesses accounting systems, procedures, and documentation to ensure compliance with federal and state grant standards. No funding or award information is present in this document.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form F Budget Narrative
data.highlights: This document is a required fillable budget narrative form for the Texas RHTP application. It instructs applicants to describe and justify their proposed budget for the grant period. It also allows applicants to request an advance payment up to 25% of the requested amount with justification.

data.title: TX - 2025 - Form E, Performance Measures
data.highlights: This applicant form requires Texas RHTP applicants to specify at least one short-term and one long-term performance measure related to project goals. All applicants must report outcomes related to reducing violence against nurses. Performance will be tracked and reported in quarterly and final project reports.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Solicitation RFA HHS0016203 Appendix B, HHSC Approved Non-Medical Drivers of Health Assessment Questions
data.highlights: This appendix provides standardized assessment questions (in English and Spanish) to evaluate Texas Medicaid members' non-medical drivers of health, covering food, transportation, housing, and child care. The questions are designed for use in the Rural Health Transformation Program to identify social determinants affecting rural beneficiaries. No funding or award information is included in this guidance.

data.title: TX - 2026 - TX - RHTP Application Preparation Resources
data.highlights: Form D is an applicant guidance form requiring each applicant to specify a timeline for their proposed project's key activities and milestones across an 18-month grant period. It is part of the Texas RHTP application package, assisting organizations in planning and documenting implementation steps for the RHTP-funded projects.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Form C – Narrative Proposal
data.highlights: This is a required narrative proposal form for applicants to describe planned violence reduction projects under the Texas RHTP. Applicants outline project approach, innovation, goals, methods, evaluation, sustainability, and baseline facility/statistical information. Focus is on addressing and reducing workplace violence against nurses in rural facilities.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Form B-1, Non-Governmental Entity – Board of Directors and Principal Officers
data.highlights: Form B-1 is used as part of the RHTP application package to provide names and roles of the applicant's board of directors and principal officers. It collects contact and ownership information for transparency and eligibility checks. No funding or programmatic activity information is included.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form B, Governmental Entity - Authorized Officials
data.highlights: This supporting application form is used to list the authorized officials empowered to sign RHTP grant agreements on behalf of an applicant. It collects names, contact information, and titles for legal/contractual purposes in the Texas RHTP program RFA package.

data.title: TX - 2026 - FORM A - FACE PAGE
data.highlights: This document is the face page form to be completed as part of the Texas Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) application package. It collects applicant facility information and the total funding amount requested for the project period April 2026 to February 2028. No award decisions or recipient data are present in this form.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Exhibit G: Exceptions Form
data.highlights: This Exhibit G: Exceptions Form, part of the Texas RHTP application packet, provides a structured template for applicants to note proposed contract exceptions or deviations from solicitation terms. It does not contain programmatic, financial, or awardee details. No completion is required if no exceptions are being taken.

data.title: TX - 2025 - Exhibit F HHS Online Bid Room Information
data.highlights: This document provides instructions for applicants to register and access the Texas HHS Online Bid Room in order to submit responses for the RHTP solicitation. It details the multi-step process for non-HHS employees to request an account, important deadlines regarding account activation, and support contact information. Key contacts: Help Desk

data.title: TX - 2024 - Exhibit E, Workplace Violence Against Nurses Evaluation Tool RFA HHS0016121 Criteria, Subcriteria Sheet
data.highlights: This guidance outlines the evaluation tool for Texas RHTP grant submissions focused on workplace violence against nurses. Criteria include demonstrated need, innovation, ability, and cost, with detailed scoring guidance to ensure projects are both impactful and sustainable. The focus is on fostering innovative and evidence-based solutions for rural health facilities.

data.title: TX - 2025 - Texas HHS System Data Use Agreement Attachment 2: Security and Privacy Inquiry (SPI)
data.highlights: This compliance form requires RHTP applicants for Texas to demonstrate that their information systems and workforce meet stringent HIPAA, privacy, and security requirements before any RHTP contract can be awarded. The document outlines required policies, technical and administrative safeguards, staff training, breach response, and documentation standards. Applicants must address all items or provide a corrective action plan before progressing in the RHTP procurement process.

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS Uniform Terms and Conditions – Grant
data.highlights:
This document sets out the required terms and conditions for all Texas Health and Human Services grant agreements, including those for RHTP. It defines allowable uses of funds, audit and reporting obligations, intellectual property provisions, and compliance requirements for grantees. These terms are incorporated into all grant agreements for RHTP subrecipients, ensuring uniform administration and oversight. Key contacts: HHSC Civil Rights Office HHSCivilRightsOffice@hhsc.state.tx.us

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form H: Internal Controls Questionnaire
data.highlights: This document is an internal controls questionnaire required as part of the application for the Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program under RHTP. It outlines financial management, administration, and accounting system requirements for grantees receiving HHSC awards. Applicants must demonstrate they have proper systems and procedures in place to manage and report award funds in compliance with federal and state standards.

data.title: TX - 2005 - Form G: Contract and Litigation History
data.highlights:
Form G is an applicant disclosure form required for the Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA and focuses on organizational integrity and conflict of interest screening. It requests applicants to disclose conflict of interest, contract history, and litigation background as mandatory parts of the application process.

Event schedule:

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form F, Subcontracting Information
data.highlights: This form is required as part of an RFA application for Texas's Maternal Health Outcomes Program and collects information on any subcontractors applicants will use to deliver direct services. It ensures applicants disclose all partners who will serve Medicaid clients, supporting program transparency and oversight.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form E: Performance Measures and Funding Ceiling Request
data.highlights:
Applicants must use this form to propose their funding ceiling and number of unduplicated maternal health outcome clients to be served. The form is required for the Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA and covers FY2026 (partial year) and FY2027. Requested funding and performance targets will be finalized through negotiation after award selection.

Event schedule:
- FY 2026 Grant Start - XX/1/2026
- FY 2027 Grant Year - 09/01/2026

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form D: Texas Counties Served by Project
data.highlights: Applicants must specify the Texas counties where they will provide Maternal Health Outcomes services and can include counties where they have existing or planned clinics, hospitals, or outreach activities. The form covers a wide range of rural and underserved counties across all major Texas regions. This distribution reflects the program's aim to ensure broad statewide rural coverage for maternal health improvements.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form C, Work Plan
data.highlights: This Form C, Work Plan outlines required applicant responses for the Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA, guiding applicants in describing their current and proposed enhancements to MHO programs. Applicants must detail existing funding, target populations, data collection, and key partnerships, with required supporting attachments. The form defines expectations for measurable program improvement and sustainability beyond the grant period.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form B-2, Nonprofit or For-Profit Entity
data.highlights: This document is a required form that requests entity and personnel information from applicants to the Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA. It collects Board of Directors, officer, and key personnel details, as well as principal ownership for for-profit organizations. No specific award, outcome, or fiscal data are included in this form.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Form A – Face Page
data.highlights: This form is the required applicant cover sheet for the Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA under RHTP. It collects essential applicant and project information, including legal entity, financial, and contact details as a condition for submitting an RFA response.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Exhibit H, Insurance Requirements
data.highlights: This exhibit details required insurance coverages for all grantees and subgrantees participating in the RHTP Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA. It sets minimum coverage amounts and types, mandates inclusion of certain clauses, and defines compliance procedures for all funded parties. No funding or awards are described in this document.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Exhibit G, Online Bid Room Information
data.highlights: This document provides instructions for applicants on how to access and use the HHS Online Bid Room to submit their RHTP Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA response. It outlines submission options, registration steps, technical requirements, and where to get help. The guidance emphasizes adherence to deadlines and system requirements to avoid disqualification.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Exhibit F, Evaluation Tool
data.highlights: This document provides the evaluation criteria and scoring rubric for applications to the Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA. It emphasizes proposed work, targeted populations with unmet needs, and effective partnerships. The tool guides reviewers in scoring program sustainability, enhancement plans, and population health impact.

data.title: TX - 2026 - EXHIBIT E: EXCEPTIONS
data.highlights: Exhibit E is the Exceptions form for the 2026 Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA in Texas, part of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) solicitation package. Respondents are instructed to disclose contract exceptions, but no program awards are listed in this document.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Exhibit B-1, HHS Additional Provisions Grant Funding
data.highlights: This exhibit details additional legal, operational, and programmatic requirements imposed on awardees of the Pediatric Tele-Connectivity Resource Program for Rural Texas for State Fiscal Year 2026, particularly for disaster response, telemedicine/telehealth service standards, and grant oversight. It reinforces requirements for care continuity, medical records management, and third-party billing, with added provisions for emergencies and turnover.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Exhibit B, HHS Uniform Terms and Conditions – Grant
data.highlights: This document outlines the terms, conditions, audit, and administrative requirements for subrecipients of the Pediatric Tele-Connectivity Resource Program for Rural Texas. It provides federal and state compliance standards, payment provisions, allowable costs, and intellectual property stipulations for awarded grantees. No budget or specific awards are included in this exhibit. Key contacts: HHSCivilRightsOffice@hhsc.state.tx.us

data.title: TX - 2019 - RFA No. HHS0016838 Exhibit D-1 Data Use Agreement Between the Texas Health and Human Services System and Contractor
data.highlights: This document is the Data Use Agreement (DUA) required for all contractors under the Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA (RHTP), specifying contractor obligations related to the use, access, safeguarding, and reporting of confidential information including PHI, PII, and Medicaid data. It establishes legal, technical, and administrative protocols aligned with HIPAA, Texas law, and federal IT standards. The DUA is foundational in ensuring recipients maintain strict privacy and security standards as part of their participation in state-funded rural health transformation initiatives.

keyDates.label: RFA No. HHS0016838 Exhibit D-1 D ATA U SE A GREEMENT B ETWEEN T HE T EXAS H EALTH A ND H UMAN S ERVICES S YSTEM AND C ONTRACTOR This Data Use Agreement (“DUA”) is effective as of the date of the Base Contract into which it is incorporated (“Effective Date”), by and between the Texas Health and Human Services System, which includes the Texas Health and Human Services Commission and the Department of State Health Services (“HHS”) and Contractor (the "Base Contract"). ARTICLE 1. PURPOSE; APPLICABILITY; ORDER OF PRECEDENCE The purpose of this DUA is to facilitate access to, creation, receipt, maintenance, use, disclosure or transmission of Confidential Information with Contractor, and describe Contractor’s rights and obligations with respect to the Confidential Information and the limited purposes for which the Contractor may create, receive, maintain, use, disclose or have access to Confidential Information. This DUA also describes HHS’s remedies in the event of Contractor’s noncompliance with its obligations under this DUA. This DUA applies to both HHS business associates, as “business associate” is defined in the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), and contractors who are not business associates, who create, receive, maintain, use, disclose or have access to Confidential Information on behalf of HHS, its programs or clients as described in the Base Contract. As a best practice, HHS requires its contractors to comply with the terms of this DUA to safeguard all types of Confidential Information. As of the Effective Date of this DUA, if any provision of the Base Contract conflicts with this DUA, this DUA controls. ARTICLE 2. DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this DUA, capitalized, underlined terms have the following meanings: “Authorized Purpose” means the specific purpose or purposes described in the Base Contract for Contractor to fulfill its obligations under the Base Contract, or any other purpose expressly authorized by HHS in writing in advance. “Authorized User” means a person: (1) Who is authorized to create, receive, maintain, have access to, process, view, handle, examine, interpret, or analyze Confidential Information pursuant to this DUA; (2) For whom Contractor warrants and represents has a demonstrable need to create, receive, maintain, use, disclose or have access to the Confidential Information; and (3) Who has agreed in writing to be bound by the disclosure and use limitations pertaining to the Confidential Information as required by this DUA. “Breach” means an impermissible use or disclosure of electronic or non-electronic sensitive personal information by an unauthorized person or for an unauthorized purpose that compromises the security or GOVERNMENTAL ENTITY VERSION HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 1 of 11

privacy of Confidential Information such that the use or disclosure poses a risk of reputational harm, theft of financial information, identity theft, or medical identity theft. Any acquisition, access, use, disclosure or loss of Confidential Information other than as permitted by this DUA shall be presumed to be a Breach unless Contractor demonstrates, based on a risk assessment, that there is a low probability that the Confidential Information has been compromised. “Confidential Information” means any communication or record (whether oral, written, electronically stored or transmitted, or in any other form) provided to or made available to Contractor or that Contractor may create, receive, maintain, use, disclose or have access to on behalf of HHS that consists of or includes any or all of the following: (1) Education records as defined in the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, 20 U.S.C. §1232g; 34 C.F.R. Part 99 (2) Federal Tax Information as defined in Internal Revenue Code §6103 and Internal Revenue Service Publication 1075; (3) Personal Identifying Information (PII) as defined in Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 521; (4) Protected Health Information (PHI) in any form including without limitation, Electronic Protected Health Information or Unsecured Protected Health Information as defined in 45 C.F.R. §160.103; (5) Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) as defined in Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 521; (6) Social Security Administration Data, including, without limitation, Medicaid information means disclosures of information made by the Social Security Administration or the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services from a federal system of records for administration of federally funded benefit programs under the Social Security Act, 42 U.S.C., Chapter 7; (7) All privileged work product; (8) All information designated as confidential under the constitution and laws of the State of Texas and of the United States, including the Texas Health & Safety Code and the Texas Public Information Act, Texas Government Code, Chapter 552. “Destroy”, “Destruction”, for Confidential Information, means: (1) Paper, film, or other hard copy media have been shredded or destroyed such that the Confidential Information cannot be read or otherwise cannot be reconstructed. Redaction is specifically excluded as a means of data destruction. (2) Electronic media have been cleared, purged, or destroyed consistent with NIST Special Publication 800-88, " Guidelines for Media Sanitization , " such that the Confidential Information cannot be retrieved. “Discover, Discovery” means the first day on which a Breach becomes known to Contractor, or, by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known to Contractor. Code § 151.002(6); Tex. H. & S. Code §166.164 (medical power of attorney); and Texas Estates Code § 22.031 (representative). “Required by Law” means a mandate contained in law that compels an entity to use or disclose Confidential Information that is enforceable in a court of law, including court orders, warrants, subpoenas or investigative demands. “Subcontractor” means a person who contracts with a prime contractor to work, to supply commodities, or to contribute toward completing work for a governmental entity. “Workforce” means employees, volunteers, trainees or other persons whose performance of work is under the direct control of a party, whether or not they are paid by that party. ARTICLE 3. C ONTRACTOR ' S DUTIES REGARDING C ONFIDENTIAL I NFORMATION Section 3.01 Obligations of Contractor Contractor agrees that: (A) With respect to PHI, Contractor shall: (1) Make PHI available in a designated record set if requested by HHS, if Contractor maintains PHI in a designated record set, as defined in HIPAA. (2) Provide to HHS data aggregation services related to the healthcare operations Contractor performs for HHS pursuant to the Base Contract, if requested by HHS, if Contractor provides data aggregation services as defined in HIPAA. (3) Provide access to PHI to an individual who is requesting his or her own PHI, or such individual’s Legally Authorized Representative, in compliance with the requirements of HIPAA. (4) Make PHI available to HHS for amendment, and incorporate any amendments to PHI that HHS directs, in compliance with HIPAA. (5) Document and make available to HHS, an accounting of disclosures in compliance with the requirements of HIPAA. (6) If Contractor receives a request for access, amendment or accounting of PHI by any individual, promptly forward the request to HHS or, if forwarding the request would violate HIPAA, promptly notify HHS of the request and of Contractor’s response. HHS will respond to all such requests, unless Contractor is Required by Law to respond or HHS has given prior written consent for Contractor to respond to and account for all such requests. (B) With respect to ALL Confidential Information, Contractor shall: (1) Exercise reasonable care and no less than the same degree of care Contractor uses to protect its own confidential, proprietary and trade secret information to prevent Confidential Information from being used in a manner that is not expressly an Authorized Purpose or as Required by Law. Contractor will access, create, maintain, receive, use, disclose, transmit or Destroy Confidential Information in a secure fashion that protects against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the security or integrity of such information or unauthorized uses . (2) Establish, implement and maintain appropriate procedural, administrative, physical and technical safeguards to preserve and maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the Confidential Information, in accordance with applicable laws or regulations relating to Confidential Information, to prevent any unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information as long as Contractor has such Confidential Information in its actual or constructive possession. (3) Implement, update as necessary, and document privacy, security and Breach notice policies and procedures and an incident response plan to address a Breach, to comply with the privacy, security and breach notice requirements of this DUA prior to conducting work under the Base Contract. All of Contractor’s Authorized Users, Workforce and Subcontractors with access to a state computer system or database will complete a cybersecurity training program certified under Texas Government Code Section 2054.519 by the Texas Department of Information Resources. (5) Establish, implement and maintain appropriate sanctions against any member of its Workforce or Subcontractor who fails to comply with this DUA, the Base Contract or applicable law. Contractor shall maintain evidence of sanctions and produce it to HHS upon request. (6) Obtain prior written approval of HHS, to disclose or provide access to any Confidential Information on the basis that such act is Required by Law, so that HHS may have the opportunity to object to the disclosure or access and seek appropriate relief. If HHS objects to such disclosure or access, Contractor shall refrain from disclosing or providing access to the Confidential Information until HHS has exhausted all alternatives for relief. (7) Certify that its Authorized Users each have a demonstrated need to know and have access to Confidential Information solely to the minimum extent necessary to accomplish the Authorized Purpose and that each has agreed in writing to be bound by the disclosure and use limitations pertaining to the Confidential Information contained in this DUA. Contractor and its Subcontractors shall maintain at all times an updated, complete, accurate list of Authorized Users and supply it to HHS upon request. (8) Provide, and shall cause its Subcontractors and agents to provide, to HHS periodic written confirmation of compliance with controls and the terms and conditions of this DUA. (9) Return to HHS or Destroy, at HHS’s election and at Contractor’s expense, all Confidential Information received from HHS or created or maintained by Contractor or any of Contractor’s agents or Subcontractors on HHS's behalf upon the termination or expiration of this DUA, if reasonably feasible and permitted by law. Contractor shall certify in writing to HHS that all such Confidential Information has been Destroyed or returned to HHS, and that Contractor and its agents and Subcontractors have retained no copies thereof. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Contractor acknowledges and agrees that it may not Destroy any Confidential Information if federal or state law, or HHS record retention policy or a litigation hold notice prohibits such Destruction. If such return or Destruction is not reasonably feasible, or is GOVERNMENTAL ENTITY VERSION HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 4 of 11

impermissible by law, Contractor shall immediately notify HHS of the reasons such return or Destruction is not feasible and agree to extend the protections of this DUA to the Confidential Information for as long as Contractor maintains such Confidential Information. (10) Complete and return with the Base Contract to HHS, attached as Attachment 2 to this DUA, the HHS Security and Privacy Initial Inquiry (SPI) at https://hhs.texas.gov/laws- regulations/forms/miscellaneous/hhs-information-security-privacy-initial-inquiry-spi . The SPI identifies basic privacy and security controls with which Contractor must comply to protect Confidential Information. Contractor shall comply with periodic security controls compliance assessment and monitoring by HHS as required by state and federal law, based on the type of Confidential Information Contractor creates, receives, maintains, uses, discloses or has access to and the Authorized Purpose and level of risk. Contractor's security controls shall be based on the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication 800-53. Contractor shall update its security controls assessment whenever there are significant changes in security controls for HHS Confidential Information and shall provide the updated document to HHS. HHS also reserves the right to request updates as needed to satisfy state and federal monitoring requirements. (11) Comply with the HHS Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) and require each Subcontractor and Workforce member who has direct access to HHS Information Resources, as defined in the AUP, to execute an HHS Acceptable Use Agreement. (12) Only conduct secure transmissions of Confidential Information whether in paper, oral or electronic form. A secure transmission of electronic Confidential Information in motion includes secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) or encryption at an appropriate level as required by rule, regulation or law. Confidential Information at rest requires encryption unless there is adequate administrative, technical, and physical security as required by rule, regulation or law. All electronic data transfer and communications of Confidential Information shall be through secure systems. Contractor shall provide proof of system, media or device security and/or encryption to HHS no later than 48 hours after HHS's written request in response to a compliance investigation, audit, or the Discovery of a Breach. HHS may also request production of proof of security at other times as necessary to satisfy state and federal monitoring requirements. Deidentification of Confidential Information in accordance with HIPAA de-identification standards is deemed secure. (13) Designate and identify a person or persons, as Privacy Official and Information Security Official, each of whom is authorized to act on behalf of Contractor and is responsible for the development and implementation of the privacy and security requirements in this DUA. Upon written notice from HHS, Contractor shall promptly remove and replace such official(s) if such official(s) is not performing the required functions. data.title: TX - 2026 - Exhibit G, Insurance Requirements
data.highlights: This document outlines insurance coverage requirements that recipients must maintain for the duration of participation in the SFY 2026 Pediatric Tele-Connectivity Resource Program for Rural Texas. Minimum coverage limits are specified for liability, errors and omissions, workers' compensation, cyber/privacy, and crime insurance. All coverage must comply with Texas Health and Human Services Commission standards and must be provided by carriers with sufficient financial ratings.

data.title: TX - 2019 - RFA No. HHS0016838 Exhibit D Data Use Agreement Between Texas Health and Human Services System and Contractor
data.highlights: This Data Use Agreement is a mandatory compliance requirement for contractors under the Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA HHS0016838. It establishes legal and procedural responsibilities for handling, protecting, and reporting breaches involving confidential information including PHI, Medicaid, and educational records. Contractors and any subcontractors must comply with HIPAA, Texas state law, and respond to breaches with rigorous protocols and documentation. Key contacts: Chief Privacy Officer privacy@hhsc.state.tx.us

keyDates.label: RFA No. HHS0016838 Exhibit D D ATA U SE A GREEMENT B ETWEEN T HE T EXAS H EALTH A ND H UMAN S ERVICES S YSTEM AND C ONTRACTOR This Data Use Agreement (“DUA”) is effective as of the date of the Base Contract into which it is incorporated (“Effective Date”), by and between the Texas Health and Human Services System, which includes the Texas Health and Human Services Commission and the Department of State Health Services (“HHS”) and Contractor (the "Base Contract"). ARTICLE 1. PURPOSE; APPLICABILITY; ORDER OF PRECEDENCE The purpose of this DUA is to facilitate access to, creation, receipt, maintenance, use, disclosure or transmission of Confidential Information with Contractor, and describe Contractor’s rights and obligations with respect to the Confidential Information and the limited purposes for which the Contractor may create, receive, maintain, use, disclose or have access to Confidential Information. This DUA also describes HHS’s remedies in the event of Contractor’s noncompliance with its obligations under this DUA. This DUA applies to both HHS business associates, as “business associate” is defined in the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), and contractors who are not business associates, who create, receive, maintain, use, disclose or have access to Confidential Information on behalf of HHS, its programs or clients as described in the Base Contract. As a best practice, HHS requires its contractors to comply with the terms of this DUA to safeguard all types of Confidential Information. As of the Effective Date of this DUA, if any provision of the Base Contract conflicts with this DUA, this DUA controls. ARTICLE 2. DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this DUA, capitalized, underlined terms have the following meanings: “Authorized Purpose” means the specific purpose or purposes described in the Base Contract for Contractor to fulfill its obligations under the Base Contract, or any other purpose expressly authorized by HHS in writing in advance. “Authorized User” means a person: (1) Who is authorized to create, receive, maintain, have access to, process, view, handle, examine, interpret, or analyze Confidential Information pursuant to this DUA; (2) For whom Contractor warrants and represents has a demonstrable need to create, receive, maintain, use, disclose or have access to the Confidential Information; and (3) Who has agreed in writing to be bound by the disclosure and use limitations pertaining to the Confidential Information as required by this DUA. “Breach” means an impermissible use or disclosure of electronic or non-electronic sensitive personal information by an unauthorized person or for an unauthorized purpose that compromises the security or privacy of Confidential Information such that the use or disclosure poses a risk of reputational harm, theft of financial information, identity theft, or medical identity theft. Any acquisition, access, use, disclosure or loss of Confidential Information other than as permitted by this HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 1 of 11

DUA shall be presumed to be a Breach unless Contractor demonstrates, based on a risk assessment, that there is a low probability that the Confidential Information has been compromised. “Confidential Information” means any communication or record (whether oral, written, electronically stored or transmitted, or in any other form) provided to or made available to Contractor or that Contractor may create, receive, maintain, use, disclose or have access to on behalf of HHS that consists of or includes any or all of the following: (1) Education records as defined in the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, 20 U.S.C. §1232g; 34 C.F.R. Part 99 (2) Federal Tax Information as defined in Internal Revenue Code §6103 and Internal Revenue Service Publication 1075; (3) Personal Identifying Information (PII) as defined in Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 521; (4) Protected Health Information (PHI) in any form including without limitation, Electronic Protected Health Information or Unsecured Protected Health Information as defined in 45 C.F.R. §160.103; (5) Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) as defined in Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 521; (6) Social Security Administration Data, including, without limitation, Medicaid information means disclosures of information made by the Social Security Administration or the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services from a federal system of records for administration of federally funded benefit programs under the Social Security Act, 42 U.S.C., Chapter 7; (7) All privileged work product; (8) All information designated as confidential under the constitution and laws of the State of Texas and of the United States, including the Texas Health & Safety Code and the Texas Public Information Act, Texas Government Code, Chapter 552. “Destroy”, “Destruction”, for Confidential Information, means: (1) Paper, film, or other hard copy media have been shredded or destroyed such that the Confidential Information cannot be read or otherwise cannot be reconstructed. Redaction is specifically excluded as a means of data destruction. (2) Electronic media have been cleared, purged, or destroyed consistent with NIST Special Publication 800-88, " Guidelines for Media Sanitization , " such that the Confidential Information cannot be retrieved. “Discover, Discovery” means the first day on which a Breach becomes known to Contractor, or, by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known to Contractor. “Legally Authorized Representative” of an individual, including as provided in 45 CFR 435.923 (authorized representative); 45 CFR 164.502(g)(1) (personal representative); Tex. Occ. Code § 151.002(6); Tex. H. & S. Code §166.164 (medical power of attorney); and Texas Estates Code § 22.031 (representative). “Required by Law” means a mandate contained in law that compels an entity to use or disclose Confidential Information that is enforceable in a court of law, including court orders, warrants, subpoenas or investigative demands. HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 2 of 11

“Subcontractor” means a person who contracts with a prime contractor to work, to supply commodities, or to contribute toward completing work for a governmental entity. “Workforce” means employees, volunteers, trainees or other persons whose performance of work is under the direct control of a party, whether or not they are paid by that party. ARTICLE 3. C ONTRACTOR ' S DUTIES REGARDING C ONFIDENTIAL I NFORMATION Section 3.01 Obligations of Contractor Contractor agrees that: (A) With respect to PHI, Contractor shall: (1) Make PHI available in a designated record set if requested by HHS, if Contractor maintains PHI in a designated record set, as defined in HIPAA. (2) Provide to HHS data aggregation services related to the healthcare operations Contractor performs for HHS pursuant to the Base Contract, if requested by HHS, if Contractor provides data aggregation services as defined in HIPAA. (3) Provide access to PHI to an individual who is requesting his or her own PHI, or such individual’s Legally Authorized Representative, in compliance with the requirements of HIPAA. (4) Make PHI available to HHS for amendment, and incorporate any amendments to PHI that HHS directs, in compliance with HIPAA. (5) Document and make available to HHS, an accounting of disclosures in compliance with the requirements of HIPAA. (6) If Contractor receives a request for access, amendment or accounting of PHI by any individual, promptly forward the request to HHS or, if forwarding the request would violate HIPAA, promptly notify HHS of the request and of Contractor’s response. HHS will respond to all such requests, unless Contractor is Required by Law to respond or HHS has given prior written consent for Contractor to respond to and account for all such requests. (B) With respect to ALL Confidential Information, Contractor shall: (1) Exercise reasonable care and no less than the same degree of care Contractor uses to protect its own confidential, proprietary and trade secret information to prevent Confidential Information from being used in a manner that is not expressly an Authorized Purpose or as Required by Law. Contractor will access, create, maintain, receive, use, disclose, transmit or Destroy Confidential Information in a secure fashion that protects against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the security or integrity of such information or unauthorized uses . (2) Establish, implement and maintain appropriate procedural, administrative, physical and technical safeguards to preserve and maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the Confidential Information, in accordance with applicable laws or regulations relating to Confidential Information, to prevent any unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information as long as Contractor has such Confidential Information in its actual or constructive possession. (3) Implement, update as necessary, and document privacy, security and Breach notice policies and procedures and an incident response plan to address a Breach, to comply with the privacy, security and breach notice requirements of this DUA prior to conducting work under the Base Contract. Contractor HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 3 of 11

shall produce, within three business days of a request by HHS, copies of its policies and procedures and records relating to the use or disclosure of Confidential Information. (4) Obtain HHS’s prior written consent to disclose or allow access to any portion of the Confidential Information to any person, other than Authorized Users, Workforce or Subcontractors of Contractor who have completed training in confidentiality, privacy, security and the importance of promptly reporting any Breach to Contractor's management and as permitted in Section 3.01(A)(3), above. Contractor shall produce evidence of completed training to HHS upon request. HHS, at its election, may assist Contractor in training and education on specific or unique HHS processes, systems and/or requirements. All of Contractor’s Authorized Users, Workforce and Subcontractors with access to a state computer system or database will complete a cybersecurity training program certified under Texas Government Code Section 2054.519 by the Texas Department of Information Resources. (5) Establish, implement and maintain appropriate sanctions against any member of its Workforce or Subcontractor who fails to comply with this DUA, the Base Contract or applicable law. Contractor shall maintain evidence of sanctions and produce it to HHS upon request. (6) Obtain prior written approval of HHS, to disclose or provide access to any Confidential Information on the basis that such act is Required by Law, so that HHS may have the opportunity to object to the disclosure or access and seek appropriate relief. If HHS objects to such disclosure or access, Contractor shall refrain from disclosing or providing access to the Confidential Information until HHS has exhausted all alternatives for relief. (7) Certify that its Authorized Users each have a demonstrated need to know and have access to Confidential Information solely to the minimum extent necessary to accomplish the Authorized Purpose and that each has agreed in writing to be bound by the disclosure and use limitations pertaining to the Confidential Information contained in this DUA. Contractor and its Subcontractors shall maintain at all times an updated, complete, accurate list of Authorized Users and supply it to HHS upon request. (8) Provide, and shall cause its Subcontractors and agents to provide, to HHS periodic written confirmation of compliance with controls and the terms and conditions of this DUA. (9) Return to HHS or Destroy, at HHS’s election and at Contractor’s expense, all Confidential Information received from HHS or created or maintained by Contractor or any of Contractor’s agents or Subcontractors on HHS's behalf upon the termination or expiration of this DUA, if reasonably feasible and permitted by law. Contractor shall certify in writing to HHS that all such Confidential Information has been Destroyed or returned to HHS, and that Contractor and its agents and Subcontractors have retained no copies thereof. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Contractor acknowledges and agrees that it may not Destroy any Confidential Information if federal or state law, or HHS record retention policy or a litigation hold notice prohibits such Destruction. If such return or Destruction is not reasonably feasible, or is impermissible by law, Contractor shall immediately notify HHS of the reasons such return or Destruction is not feasible and agree to extend the protections of this DUA to the Confidential Information for as long as Contractor maintains such Confidential Information. (10) Complete and return with the Base Contract to HHS, attached as Attachment 2 to this DUA, the HHS Security and Privacy Initial Inquiry (SPI) at https://hhs.texas.gov/laws- regulations/forms/miscellaneous/hhs-information-security-privacy-initial-inquiry-spi . The SPI identifies basic privacy and security controls with which Contractor must comply to protect Confidential Information. Contractor shall comply with periodic security controls compliance assessment and monitoring by HHS as required by state and federal law, based on the type of Confidential Information Contractor creates, receives, maintains, uses, discloses or has access to and the Authorized Purpose and level of risk. Contractor's HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 4 of 11

security controls shall be based on the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication 800-53. Contractor shall update its security controls assessment whenever there are significant changes in security controls for HHS Confidential Information and shall provide the updated document to HHS. HHS also reserves the right to request updates as needed to satisfy state and federal monitoring requirements. (11) Comply with the HHS Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) and require each Subcontractor and Workforce member who has direct access to HHS Information Resources, as defined in the AUP, to execute an HHS Acceptable Use Agreement. (12) Only conduct secure transmissions of Confidential Information whether in paper, oral or electronic form. A secure transmission of electronic Confidential Information in motion includes secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) or encryption at an appropriate level as required by rule, regulation or law. Confidential Information at rest requires encryption unless there is adequate administrative, technical, and physical security as required by rule, regulation or law. All electronic data transfer and communications of Confidential Information shall be through secure systems. Contractor shall provide proof of system, media or device security and/or encryption to HHS no later than 48 hours after HHS's written request in response to a compliance investigation, audit, or the Discovery of a Breach. HHS may also request production of proof of security at other times as necessary to satisfy state and federal monitoring requirements. Deidentification of Confidential Information in accordance with HIPAA de-identification standards is deemed secure. (13) Designate and identify a person or persons, as Privacy Official and Information Security Official, each of whom is authorized to act on behalf of Contractor and is responsible for the development and implementation of the privacy and security requirements in this DUA. Contractor shall provide name and current address, phone number and e-mail address for such designated officials to HHS upon execution of this DUA and prior to any change. Upon written notice from HHS, Contractor shall promptly remove and replace such official(s) if such official(s) is not performing the required functions. (14) Make available to HHS any information HHS requires to fulfill HHS's obligations to provide access to, or copies of, Confidential Information in accordance with applicable laws, regulations or demands of a regulatory authority relating to Confidential Information. Contractor shall provide such information in a time and manner reasonably agreed upon or as designated by the applicable law or regulatory authority. (15) Comply with the following laws and standards if applicable to the type of Confidential Information and Contractor's Authorized Purpose : • Title 1, Part 10, Chapter 202, Subchapter B , Texas Administrative Code; • The Privacy Act of 1974; • OMB Memorandum 17-12; • The Federal Information Security Management Act of 2002 (FISMA); • The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA); • Internal Revenue Publication 1075 – Tax Information Security Guidelines for Federal, State and Local Agencies; • National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication 800-66 Revision 1 – An Introductory Resource Guide for Implementing the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Security Rule; HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 5 of 11

• NIST Special Publications 800-53 a nd 800-53A – Recommended Security Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations, as currently revised; • NIST Special Publication 800-47 – Security Guide for Interconnecting Information Technology Systems; • NIST Special Publication 800-88, Guidelines for Media Sanitization ; • NIST Special Publication 800-111, Guide to Storage of Encryption Technologies for End User Devices containing PHI; • Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act • Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 521; • Any other State or Federal law, regulation, or administrative rule relating to the specific HHS program area that Contractor supports on behalf of HHS. (16) Be permitted to use or disclose Confidential Information for the proper management and administration of Contractor or to carry out Contractor’s legal responsibilities, except as otherwise limited by this DUA, the Base Contract, or law applicable to the Confidential Information, if: (a) Disclosure is Required by Law; (b) Contractor obtains reasonable assurances from the person to whom the information is disclosed that the person shall: 1. Maintain the confidentiality of the Confidential Information in accordance with this DUA; 2. Use or further disclose the information only as Required by Law or for the Authorized Purpose for which it was disclosed to the person; and 3. Notify Contractor in accordance with Section 4.01 of a Breach of Confidential Information that the person Discovers or should have Discovered with the exercise of reasonable diligence. (C) With respect to ALL Confidential Information, Contractor shall NOT: (1) Attempt to re-identify or further identify Confidential Information that has been deidentified, or attempt to contact any persons whose records are contained in the Confidential Information, except for an Authorized Purpose, without express written authorization from HHS. (2) Engage in prohibited marketing or sale of Confidential Information. (3) Permit, or enter into any agreement with a Subcontractor to, create, receive, maintain, use, disclose, have access to or transmit Confidential Information, on behalf of HHS without requiring that Subcontractor first execute either the Form Subcontractor Agreement, Attachment 1, or Contractor’s own Subcontractor agreement that ensures that the Subcontractor shall comply with the same safeguards and restrictions contained in this DUA for Confidential Information. Contractor is directly responsible for its Subcontractors’ compliance with, and enforcement of, this DUA. HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 6 of 11

ARTICLE 4. BREACH NOTICE, REPORTING AND CORRECTION REQUIREMENTS Section 4.01. Cooperation and Financial Responsibility. (A) Contractor shall, at Contractor’s expense, cooperate fully with HHS in investigating, mitigating to the extent practicable, and issuing notifications as directed by HHS, for any Breach of Confidential Information. (B) Contractor shall make Confidential Information in Contractor’s possession available pursuant to the requirements of HIPAA or other applicable law upon a determination of a Breach. (C) Contractor’s obligation begins at the Discovery of a Breach and continues as long as related activity continues, until all effects of the Breach are mitigated to HHS’s satisfaction (the "incident response period"). Section 4.02. Initial Breach Notice. For federal information obtained from a federal system of records , including Federal Tax Information and Social Security Administration Data (which includes Medicaid and other governmental benefit program Confidential Information), Contractor shall notify HHS of the Breach within the first consecutive clock hour of Discovery. The Base Contract shall specify whether Confidential Information is obtained from a federal system of records. For all other types of Confidential Information Contractor shall notify HHS of the Breach not more than 24 hours after Discovery, or in a timeframe otherwise approved by HHS in writing. Contractor shall initially report to HHS's Privacy and Security Officers via email at: privacy@HHSC.state.tx.us and to the HHS division responsible for the Base Contract. Contractor shall report all information reasonably available to Contractor about the Breach. Contractor shall provide contact information to HHS for Contractor's single point of contact who will communicate with HHS both on and off business hours during the incident response period. Section 4.03 Third Business Day Notice : No later than 5 p.m. on the third business day after Discovery, or a time within which Discovery reasonably should have been made by Contractor of a Breach of Confidential Information, Contractor shall provide written notification to HHS of all reasonably available information about the Breach, and Contractor's investigation, including, to the extent known to Contractor : a. The date the Breach occurred; b. The date of Contractor's and, if applicable, Subcontractor's Discovery; c. A brief description of the Breach, including how it occurred and who is responsible (or hypotheses, if not yet determined); d. A brief description of Contractor's investigation and the status of the investigation; e. A description of the types and amount of Confidential Information involved; f. Identification of and number of all individuals reasonably believed to be affected, including first and last name of the individual and if applicable, the Legally authorized representative, last known address, age, telephone number, and email address if it is a preferred contact method; g. Contractor’s initial risk assessment of the Breach demonstrating whether individual or other notices are required by applicable law or this DUA for HHS approval, including an analysis of whether there is a low probability of compromise of the Confidential Information or whether any legal exceptions to notification apply; h. Contractor's recommendation for HHS’s approval as to the steps individuals and/or Contractor on behalf of individuals, should take to protect the individuals from potential harm, including HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 7 of 11

(A) Contractor shall immediately conduct a full and complete investigation, respond to the Breach, commit necessary and appropriate staff and resources to expeditiously respond, and report as required to HHS for incident response purposes and for purposes of HHS’s compliance with report and notification requirements, to the satisfaction of HHS. Section 4.05. Breach Notification to Individuals and Reporting to Authorities. (A) HHS may direct Contractor to provide Breach notification to individuals, regulators or third-parties, as specified by HHS following a Breach. (B) Contractor must comply with all applicable legal and regulatory requirements in the time, manner and content of any notification to individuals, regulators or third-parties, or any notice required by other state or federal authorities, including without limitation, notifications required by Texas Business and Commerce Code, Chapter 521.053(b) and HIPAA. Notice letters will be in Contractor's name and on Contractor's letterhead, unless otherwise directed by HHS, and will contain contact information, including the name and title of Contractor's representative, an email address and a toll-free telephone number, for the individual to obtain additional information. data.title: TX - 2026 - Exhibit F, Pedi-Tele Evaluation Tool
data.highlights: This evaluation tool outlines the detailed scoring criteria for applicants to the Pediatric Tele-Connectivity Resource Program for Rural Texas, focusing on cohesive project plans to link rural hospitals and clinics with pediatric telemedicine specialists. Major criteria include project approach, partnership capacity, anticipated benefits, scalability and sustainability, and a robust, reasonable budget. The framework ensures that funded projects demonstrate sustainability and impactful, statewide rural reach.

data.title: TX - 2024 - RFA No. HHS0016838 Exhibit B Health and Human Services (HHS) Uniform Terms and Conditions - Grant
data.highlights: This supporting document (Exhibit B) outlines grant terms and compliance requirements for entities applying to the Texas Maternal Health Outcomes Program RFA, part of the Rural Health Transformation Program. It includes definitions, allowable costs, audit requirements, ownership of work product, and other uniform terms to be incorporated by reference into Grants awarded under this RFA. It is not a procurement, award, or solicitation document on its own. Key contacts: HHSC Civil Rights Office HHSCivilRightsOffice@hhsc.state.tx.us

keyDates.label: ARTICLE I. data.title: IN - 2026 - Scope of Work: Lead Testing Quality Improvement (QI) Engagement
data.highlights:
This initiative uses a structured quality improvement model to increase lead screening rates among children in Indiana, focusing particularly on children at key age milestones. The program features provider incentives, training sessions, and data-driven feedback to continuously improve lead testing and reporting. Education resources and counseling are aimed at raising awareness among patients and caregivers.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Exhibit C, Texas Uniform General Conditions for Construction Contracts and 2025 Supplemental General Conditions
data.highlights: This document sets the uniform legal, safety, quality, and operational conditions for construction projects funded under the Pediatric Tele-Connectivity Resource Program for Rural Texas. It covers wage, labor, permitting, safety, quality control, project closeout, and requirements for historically underutilized businesses. As a supporting exhibit, it standardizes expectations for all construction activities under this RFA.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Form V, Appropriate Use Criteria
data.highlights: This guidance outlines appropriate use criteria for rural hospitals funded under the Texas Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program. Specific clinical criteria, including psychiatric, acute, and chronic medical condition screening, are detailed to support safe admissions and transfers. The document emphasizes hospital capacity, stabilization, and patient rights for treatment in the least restrictive settings.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Form U, Unusual Incident Summary Reporting Form
data.highlights: This form is part of the required reporting process for rural hospitals applying to the Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program in Texas. It is used to document and report unusual incidents such as death, abuse, neglect, or unethical conduct. The reporting ensures accountability and patient safety within rural mental health settings.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Form Q, Notification and Transfer of Forensic Patients Requiring Extended Mental Health Treatment
data.highlights: This guidance document details the notification and transfer procedures for contracted hospitals recommending extended mental health commitment for forensic patients. It establishes clear timeframes and documentation requirements to ensure timely transitions and continuity of care. The process involves collaboration between contracted hospitals, the Continuity of Services Manager, and receiving state hospitals.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Form P, Forensic Admission Referral and Coordination Processes, Roles & Responsibilities for Regional Hospitals Serving Non-Maximum Security Forensic Patients
data.highlights: This guidance describes the procedures and roles for courts, HHSC clearinghouse staff, and regional hospitals in admitting non-maximum security forensic patients. Key protocols include timely documentation transfer, admissions queue management, and collaboration between counties and rural hospitals to ensure appropriate placement and transport. The guidance supports process consistency and aims to reduce wait times for forensic mental health services. Key contacts: forensicadmissions@hhsc.state.tx.us

data.title: TX - 2024 - Form N, Crisis Service Standards
data.highlights: This document provides comprehensive operational standards and definitions for crisis services under the Texas Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program. It sets staffing, training, response timeframes, and accreditation requirements for Crisis hotlines and Mobile Crisis Outreach Teams (MCOTs), with special provisions for rural areas such as adjusted staffing and telehealth deployment. The standards also integrate suicide/homicide risk screening, continuity of care, and collaboration with emergency services for rural counties.

data.title: TX - 2005 - Form K, Litigation And Contract History
data.highlights:
This supporting document ensures that applicants for the Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program disclose information related to board membership, nonprofit status, conflicts of interest, litigation, and contract history. Responses are used for screening and evaluating applications to enhance program oversight and integrity in grant selection. No award or recipient information is contained within this specific form.

data.title: TX - 2024 - FORM G, APPLICANT EXPERIENCE
data.highlights: Form G collects detailed applicant experience for rural mental health project implementation, state and federal grant administration, data reporting, and key staff roles. It supports the Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program application and helps evaluate applicant capacity.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Form F, Project Design
data.highlights: Form F guides applicants to describe their approach to meeting strategic behavioral health gaps in rural Texas, emphasizing access, workforce, crisis response, and interagency coordination. Applicants must outline evidence-based activities, community partnerships, robust project oversight, and disaster response strategies. Special attention is given to trauma-informed care and culturally/linguistically appropriate service provision.

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0014211 Form E, Community Need
data.highlights: This document is a required application form within Texas' Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program solicitation, guiding applicants to describe local behavioral health gaps, community partner involvement, and collaborative strategies for improved rural mental health care. No award amounts or recipients are specified in this form.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Form D, Proposed Project Summary
data.highlights: Form D is the required summary worksheet for applicants proposing rural mental health projects under Texas HHS RFA HHS0014211. Applicants must summarize project scope, intended counties served, and expected outcomes, and indicate whether the project is new, scalable, or based on evidence practices.

data.title: TX - 2024 - FORM C, FINANCIAL CONTROLS
data.highlights: Applicants are required to provide detailed financial management information and documentation, including the use of computerized, manual, or mixed accounting systems, as well as written policies. Monthly expenditure and match reports are mandated, and compliance with federal and state standards is emphasized. Volunteers may be used as match if documentation meets state standards.

data.title: TX - 2005 - Form B, Administrative Information
data.highlights:
This form collects required administrative, conflict of interest, and entity status disclosures from applicants to the Texas Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program. It is a key part of the RFA submission package, supporting screening for eligibility and organizational compliance. No funding amounts, timelines, or implementation details are present in this document.

Event schedule:

keyDates.label: Assessed a penalty in a federal civil administrative enforcement action in connection with a contract awarded by the federal government for relief, recovery or reconstruction efforts as a result of Hurricanes Rita or Katrina or any other disaster occurring after , 2005 under Government Code 2261.053?

data.title: TX - 2024 - FORM A, APPLICANT INFORMATION
data.highlights: This is the standard applicant information form required for organizations applying to the Texas Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program. It collects details on the organizational lead, entity type, and contact information as part of the RFA package.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Exhibit N, Outpatient Competency Restoration Statement of Work
data.highlights: This document details the Statement of Work for Outpatient Competency Restoration programs under the Texas Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program. Grantees must provide comprehensive community-based forensic mental health services in rural areas, partnering with local authorities and meeting strict reporting and outcome targets. A required local cash or in-kind match (25% or 50% depending on county size) applies to grant funds.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Exhibit M, Inpatient Competency Statement of Work
data.highlights: This Statement of Work defines requirements for grantees providing inpatient forensic psychiatric competency restoration services for adults in rural Texas counties. Grantees must partner with licensed psychiatric hospitals, maintain specified clinical and operational standards, and meet compliance with state and federal laws. Match funding is required, with ratios depending on county population, and regular reporting and performance targets (such as restoration rates and occupancy) are detailed. Key contacts: MHContracts@hhsc.state.tx.us; crisisservices@hhs.texas.gov

data.title: TX - 2024 - EXHIBIT L, Contracted Private Beds (CPB) Statement of Work
data.highlights:
This Statement of Work provides detailed guidance for grantees under the Texas Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program to deliver inpatient psychiatric hospital services in rural areas. It specifies licensure, accreditation, match requirements, performance measures, trauma-informed care, and reporting obligations. Collaboration with local mental health authorities is mandated, and grantees must ensure culturally responsive and evidence-based service delivery. Key contacts: mhcontracts@hhsc.state.tx.us

Event schedule:

- Policies and Procedures Submission Due
- Quarterly Performance Report Due

data.title: TX - 2024 - Exhibit K, Diversion Center Statement of Work
data.highlights: This Statement of Work details operational, staffing, service, and reporting standards for grantees under Texas's Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program (RIGP) to establish or expand Diversion Centers. These centers aim to provide 24/7 crisis evaluation as alternatives to jail for adults experiencing behavioral health crises in rural counties. Requirements address trauma-informed care, community collaboration, law enforcement coordination, data reporting, and ongoing quality management. Key contacts: N/A HHSCForensicsAndJailDiversionServices@hhs.texas.gov

data.title: TX - 2024 - Exhibit J, Behavioral Health Center Statement Of Work
data.highlights: This Statement of Work sets programmatic and performance requirements for grantees establishing or expanding regional behavioral health centers in rural Texas counties. Grantees must provide outpatient mental health and substance use services for children and adults, leveraging both in-person and telehealth modalities. The document also details reporting requirements and match obligations based on county population.

data.title: TX - 2024 - BHS Matching Grants Performance Measures
data.highlights: This guidance document establishes mandatory output and outcome performance measures for Texas rural mental health grant recipients under the 2024 Rural Mental Health Initiative. Measures include participant count, retention, symptom improvement for multiple behavioral health conditions, reduced hospitalizations, reduced justice involvement, enhanced employment and housing stability, and training activities. Required demographic and assessment tools are outlined, emphasizing use of standardized instruments for consistent statewide reporting. Key contacts: BHSGrants@HHS.Texas.gov

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0014211 Request for Applications Exhibit G
data.highlights: This supporting document explains how to use the HHS Online Bid Room to submit responses for the Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program solicitation. It provides step-by-step instructions related to application submission, registration, and technical support. Key contacts: pcsbids@hhsc.state.tx.us

data.title: TX - 2024 - Exhibit F, Evaluation Tool Rural Initiative Grant Program Criteria, Subcriteria Sheet
data.highlights: This document outlines the evaluation criteria for the Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program RFA. Applicants are scored on community need, project design, ability to execute, and proposed project costs, with specific emphasis on trauma-informed, person-centered, and culturally competent approaches, partnerships, project oversight, and staffing plans.

data.title: TX - 2024 - EXHIBIT E: EXCEPTIONS
data.highlights: This is Exhibit E (Exceptions) for applicants responding to the 2024 Texas Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant RFA. It allows prospective applicants to document any exceptions to the solicitation terms as part of their application; no exceptions become part of any contract unless expressly accepted by the state in writing. No budget, policy, or program content is included in this exhibit.

data.title: TX - 2054 - HHS0014211 Request for Applications Exhibit D-3 Attachment D Data Use Agreement
data.highlights: The Data Use Agreement (DUA) sets requirements for contractors and subcontractors engaged with the Rural Mental Health Initiative Program to protect confidential information under HIPAA, Texas law, and federal standards. Contractors must implement strict privacy, security, incident response, and breach notification procedures, with reporting obligations to Texas HHS. Subcontractors are also bound by identical DUA terms. Key contacts: Privacy Officer (as designated by contractor, subject to HHS approval) privacy@hhsc.state.tx.us; Information Security Official (as designated by contractor, subject to HHS approval) infosecurity@hhsc.state.tx.us

data.title: TX - 2019 - HHS0014211 Request for Applications Exhibit D-1 Data Use Agreement Between the Texas Health and Human Services System and Contractor
data.highlights: This Data Use Agreement (DUA) defines privacy and security obligations for contractors handling confidential information as part of the Texas Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program. It explains contractor duties for managing, securing, reporting, and mitigating breaches of protected data, and is incorporated into every grant contract awarded through this RFA. (A) Contractor shall, at Contractor’s expense, cooperate fully with HHS in investigating, mitigating to the extent practicable, and issuing notifications as directed by HHS, for any Breach of Confidential Information. (B) Contractor shall make Confidential Information in Contractor’s possession available pursuant to the requirements of HIPAA or other applicable law upon a determination of a Breach. (C) Contractor’s obligation begins at the Discovery of a Breach and continues as long as related activity continues, until all effects of the Breach are mitigated to HHS’s satisfaction (the "incident response period"). Section 4.02. Initial Breach Notice. For federal information obtained from a federal system of records , including Federal Tax Information and Social Security Administration Data (which includes Medicaid and other governmental benefit program Confidential Information), Contractor shall notify HHS of the Breach within the first consecutive clock hour of Discovery. The Base Contract shall specify whether Confidential Information is obtained from a federal system of records. For all other types of Confidential Information Contractor shall notify HHS of the Breach not more than 24 hours after Discovery, or in a timeframe otherwise approved by HHS in writing. Contractor shall initially report to HHS's Privacy and Security Officers via email at: privacy@HHSC.state.tx.us and to the HHS division responsible for the Base Contract. Contractor shall report all information reasonably available to Contractor about the Breach. Contractor shall provide contact information to HHS for Contractor's single point of contact who will communicate with HHS both on and off business hours during the incident response period. Section 4.03 Third Business Day Notice : No later than 5 p.m. on the third business day after Discovery, or a time within which Discovery reasonably should have been made by Contractor of a Breach of Confidential Information, Contractor shall provide written notification to HHS of all reasonably available information about the Breach, and Contractor's investigation, including, to the extent known to Contractor : a. The date the Breach occurred; b. The date of Contractor's and, if applicable, Subcontractor's Discovery; c. A brief description of the Breach, including how it occurred and who is responsible (or hypotheses, if not yet determined); d. A brief description of Contractor's investigation and the status of the investigation; e. A description of the types and amount of Confidential Information involved; f. Identification of and number of all individuals reasonably believed to be affected, including first and last name of the individual and if applicable, the Legally authorized representative, last known address, age, telephone number, and email address if it is a preferred contact method; g. Contractor’s initial risk assessment of the Breach demonstrating whether individual or other notices are required by applicable law or this DUA for HHS approval, including an analysis of whether there is a low probability of compromise of the Confidential Information or whether any legal exceptions to notification apply; h. Contractor's recommendation for HHS’s approval as to the steps individuals and/or Contractor on behalf of individuals, should take to protect the individuals from potential harm, including HHS Data Use Agreement v.8.5 , 2019 7 of 11

data.title: TX - 2024 - HHS0014211 Request for Applications Exhibit C Health and Human Services Additional Provisions – Grant Funding
data.highlights: This document outlines additional provisions, terms, and grant conditions for applicants to the Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program in Texas. Key elements cover turnover plans, assistance in closing out grants and transferring obligations, interim extension in disaster events, and duplication of funding. The guidance ensures minimal disruption and compliance for rural mental health grant operations.

This document provides the full uniform grant terms and conditions applicable to Texas HHS grant agreements, including those under the Rural Health Transformation Program and the Rural Mental Health Initiative Grant Program. It covers standard administrative, legal, and financial requirements for grantees, as well as intellectual property, payment, audit, and compliance terms. It is incorporated by reference into all funding agreements under the related solicitation. Key contacts: HHSC Civil Rights Office HHSCivilRightsOffice@hhsc.state.tx.us
