data.highlights:
The program is funded with $203,404,327 in the first year and was approved by CMS after Alabama developed a comprehensive rural health strategy. It includes 11 initiatives such as EHR and cybersecurity, maternal and fetal health, workforce development, cancer digital regionalization, EMS enhancements, mental health, and community medicine. The Alabama Rural Health Transformation Advisory Group was established to advise on implementation and oversight.

data.title: WV - 2025 - West Virginia RHT (WV RHT) Program (02_WV_Project_Narrative_vF)
data.highlights: West Virginia’s RHT Program application outlines a comprehensive, multi-pronged plan for rural health transformation focused on improving outcomes, reducing chronic disease burdens, and revitalizing rural economies. The initiative targets high-need rural populations, aims to leverage technology, workforce innovation, prevention, and improved access, and proposes state policy changes and new funding models. Key innovations include seven flagship initiatives for technology integration, workforce pipeline development, EMS and telemedicine, with attention to maternal health, SUD, broadband, and food insecurity.

data.title: WV - 2025 - West Virginia RHT (WV RHT) Program (01_WV_Project_Abstract_vF)
data.highlights: The WV RHT Program launches a comprehensive statewide strategic plan investing $1 billion to transform rural health and workforce outcomes via seven flagship initiatives including telehealth, workforce training, payment modernization, and health innovation. This effort aims to reverse decades-long health and economic challenges in West Virginia.

Significant community, provider, and stakeholder engagement is evidenced through these endorsements.

data.title: SD - 2026 - South Dakota RHTP
data.highlights: South Dakota was awarded approximately $189.4M in FY2026 under the Rural Health Transformation Program, with a comprehensive, state-led strategy targeting rural hospital stabilization, Medicaid payment transformation, digital health infrastructure, and rural workforce expansion. Core initiatives include health IT modernization, alternative payment models, EMS regionalization, expanded maternal and behavioral health services, and workforce recruitment and retention efforts. The program directly addresses rural health disparities across all 64 rural counties, including Tribal and frontier populations.

data.title: SD - 2026 - Legislative one-pager
data.highlights: South Dakota received a $189.4M Year 1 federal award under the Rural Health Transformation Program focused on ten strategic initiatives to strengthen rural healthcare systems through technology, workforce development, care coordination, and regional EMS and behavioral health systems. The program was developed with extensive stakeholder engagement and aims for sustainable improvements over a five-year period.

data.title: SD - 2026 - South Dakota RHT Project (CCBHC/Collaborative Care Initiative)
data.highlights: South Dakota has launched a comprehensive initiative to transform behavioral health care for rural and frontier populations with a nearly $190 million federal award. The project is focused on implementing the CCBHC and Collaborative Care models, expanding crisis care capacity, and integrating physical and behavioral health systems. Early-phase goals include certifying clinics, developing payment models, and establishing quality assurance and data systems.

data.title: SD - 2026 - South Dakota RHT Project – Digital Health Modernization and Technology Grant Program
data.highlights: South Dakota received over $189 million in FY2026 for the Rural Health Transformation Project, with a major focus on digital health modernization for rural and underserved healthcare providers. Approximately $89.4 million will be available for the first grant period in 2026, with competitive sub-grants planned for electronic health records, interoperability, digital equipment, security, workforce training, and regional innovation. No individual recipient awards have yet been made; sub-grant opportunities will be detailed in the forthcoming RFA.

data.title: SD - 2026 - View South Dakota Funding Opportunities Download Funding Tips Sheet
data.highlights: The program includes initiatives such as Medicaid Primary Accountable Care Transformation, expanding the community health worker workforce, and strengthening chronic disease management. Funding opportunities and resources like webinars and fact sheets are provided to assist stakeholders. The South Dakota Department of Health administers the program from Pierre, SD.

data.highlights: This notification confirms New Hampshire's successful receipt of an RHTP award from CMS and announces the establishment of GO-NORTH to coordinate implementation. It also serves as a listserv notification regarding future updates and releases.

data.title: NH - 2026 - RHTP - New Hampshire
data.highlights: New Hampshire received the highest RHTP federal award in New England: $204M to transform rural health and Medicaid delivery. GO-NORTH leads implementation with DHHS support, emphasizing sustainable investments, workforce expansion, technology adoption, and behavioral health infrastructure. Contracting with facilitating organizations and meeting key milestones influences ongoing federal funding and overall program success.

data.title: NH - 2026 - RHTP (Granite Strong. Future Ready.)
data.highlights: New Hampshire was awarded $204 million for Budget Period 1 under the Rural Health Transformation Program. The program, branded 'Granite Strong. Future Ready.', aims to improve quality of life and health equity through investments in access to care, workforce development, innovative technology, and sustainable rural hospital financing. The GO-NORTH office will oversee implementation, partner with DHHS, and contract with subrecipients, with fiscal responsibility for expending funds quickly to meet CMS requirements.

data.title: NH - 2026 - New Hampshire RHT Plan (NHRHTP)
data.highlights: The University System of New Hampshire received a $97 million sole-source RHTP contract to build rural health workforce pathways, career ladders, and expand simulation-based clinical training infrastructure. Program priorities include high-need fields like nursing, behavioral health, maternal, dental, substance use/emergency care, and rural hospital recruitment and retention. The initiative targets statewide impact and is tied to CMS milestones and rural service obligations.

data.title: NH - 2026 - Coordination and Support for CMHCs/CCBHCs under New Hampshire's RHT Plan (RHTP)
data.highlights: The State of New Hampshire was awarded $131.6M in 100% federal funds to strengthen and modernize its behavioral health system in rural areas through coordinated statewide investments. The sole recipient, NH Community Behavioral Health Association, will lead implementation of a common EHR platform among all CMHCs, transition to CCBHC status, expand the workforce, and centralize services. The initiative includes quarterly and monthly performance monitoring, technology adoption, and workforce commitments to serve rural areas for at least five years.

data.title: NH - 2026 - New Hampshire RHTP (NHRHTP)
data.highlights: New Hampshire was awarded $204M from CMS under RHTP, with $96.9M contracted to the University System of NH to implement the state’s rural health workforce transformation, including scholarships, workforce supports, and a federated statewide clinical simulation education network. Key programs feature the Governor’s Health Awards Program to recruit and retain rural providers and major investments in regional/mobile simulation training hubs enhancing rural health capacity. The effort targets behavioral health, maternal health, dental, primary care, EMS, and substance use disorder, completely integrating workforce and clinical simulation innovation.

data.title: NH - 2026 - Foundation for Healthy Communities (FHC).pdf
data.highlights: New Hampshire was awarded $204M under CMS’s Rural Health Transformation Program and is contracting with the Foundation for Healthy Communities for implementation support of the first $66.5M budget period. The program will coordinate investments in rural care access, workforce, care models, and technology. The award ensures New Hampshire aligns with CMS milestones to maintain and expand federal support for rural transformation.

data.title: NH - 2026 - Community Development Finance Authority (CDFA).pdf

The CDFA contract starts at $43.8 million for the first budget period to launch a multi-year statewide rural health and capital improvement grant program. The program funds minor infrastructure, equipment, and facility renovation in rural hospitals, clinics, and childcare/community sites.

data.title: NH - 2026 - RHTP (NH RHTP Workforce Initiative)
data.highlights: This award funds the Community College System of New Hampshire to implement a major rural health workforce transformation under the state’s RHTP. Initiatives include regional Healthcare Career Guidance Hubs, expansion of clinical apprenticeships, a new paraprofessional training academy, and delivery of mobile SIM Lab training statewide. The efforts are designed to build rural healthcare career pathways, address workforce shortages, and ensure long-term system sustainability.

data.title: NH - 2026 - New Hampshire RHTP (771172)
data.highlights: New Hampshire received over $204 million in the first RHTP annual award from CMS. A major contract funds the New Hampshire Community Behavioral Health Association to modernize behavioral health infrastructure, EHRs, and workforce capacity, transition to the CCBHC model, and expand access across rural NH. This major investment targets population health, workforce development, and health information technology for New Hampshire’s rural mental health system.

data.title: NH - 2025 - RHTP - New Hampshire (nh-rhtc-project-narrative)
data.highlights: New Hampshire’s Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) focuses on overcoming substantial rural health challenges such as geographic barriers, provider shortages, and higher disease and behavioral health burdens compared to urban regions. The strategy emphasizes technology modernization, workforce development, innovative care and payment models, and coordinated statewide frameworks to sustainably improve health access, outcomes, and equity for rural residents. EMS deserts, maternity care shortages, and food insecurity in rural regions are directly targeted, with integrated efforts spanning prevention, data sharing, workforce, and community partnerships.

data.highlights: California awarded nearly $300 million in zero-percent interest loans to 17 financially distressed community hospitals under the Distressed Hospital Loan Program to support their operational stability. Loans have a 72-month repayment term with an 18-month grace period and are intended to prevent hospital closures and sustain care services.

data.title: CA - 2026 - RHTP Improving Access, Quality and Sustainability of Rural Healthcare Presenters: Hovik Khosrovian, Senior Policy Advisor Tyfany Frazier, Rural Health Specialist
data.highlights: This guidance document outlines California's approach and timeline for participation in the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), a $50 billion federal initiative (2026-2030) focused on rural hospital and provider transformation. It summarizes demographic trends, describes core challenges facing rural healthcare, and details activities and goals required as part of the state's RHTP application process. No awards to sub-recipients are announced; information is at the guidance and state-allocation planning level.

data.title: CA - 2026 - California RHT (CalRHT) Program Briefing
data.highlights:
California was awarded over $233 million by CMS for the Rural Health Transformation Program’s first budget period (2026). Hundreds of stakeholders were engaged to set key priorities including workforce, telehealth, and hospital stability. The CalRHT vision is a patient-centered, connected rural health system supported by workforce, technology, and care model innovation. Key contacts: CalRHT@hcai.ca.gov

data.title: OR - 2025 - Oregon Health Authority 2025-27 Governor’s Budget
data.highlights: The 2025-27 Governor’s Budget for Oregon Health Authority totals $39.6 billion, with a significant increase in General Fund and continued high federal investment. The budget prioritizes ending behavioral health workforce shortages, maintaining record Medicaid coverage, and eliminating health inequities by 2030. Strategic goals emphasize behavioral health, population health, equity, and expansion of culturally responsive providers and services.

data.title: OR - 2025 - Oregon Health Authority RHT and Medicaid Initiatives
data.highlights: The 2025-27 Agency Request Budget includes $39.0 billion in total funds, major investments in behavioral health, Medicaid coverage, workforce expansion, and public health modernization. Rural and coastal regions are specifically mentioned as focus areas for health system and workforce stability. The plan prioritizes health equity, affordable care access, and system transformation, with detailed strategies and goals through 2030.

data.title: OR - 2025 - 2025-27 Budget Summary For OHA's Legislatively Approved Budget, Spring 2026
data.highlights: Oregon's 2025–27 budget includes a $345.2 million federal funds allocation and 35 positions for the Rural Health Transformation Program, more than doubling its budget compared to the prior cycle. These funds are intended to be distributed as grants to rural communities. Budget adjustments addressed Medicaid caseloads, with no cuts to existing positions or core programming.

data.title: OR - 2026 - RHTP Catalyst Awards
data.highlights: This document details Oregon's Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) Catalyst Awards Request for Grant Proposals. Oregon will receive $197.3 million in 2026 under RHTP, to fund rural system transformation projects such as network development, workforce initiatives, technological upgrades, and tribal health. The document provides application instructions, timelines, eligibility, and budget requirements for the RFGP.

data.title: WV - 2026 - West Virginia RHTP (WV_RHTP_Frequently_Asked_Questions)
data.highlights: West Virginia received a $199.5M CMS RHTP award for FY2026, supporting a comprehensive state transformation plan with seven flagship initiatives covering virtual care access, rural workforce, health technology innovation, and more. Awards to subrecipients will be distributed by competitive processes under specific program pillars. Strategic priorities include addressing workforce barriers, establishing WV as a rural health innovation center, and improving system sustainability and health outcomes. Multiple rural chronic diseases and behavioral health are high priorities.

data.title: NV - 2026 - RHTP, Workforce Recruitment & Rural Access Program (WRRAP), Graduate Medical Education (GME) Program, Statewide Healthcare Access and Recruitment Program (SHARP)
data.highlights: Nevada received over $179 million in federal Rural Health Transformation Program funds to launch the Workforce Recruitment & Rural Access Program, focused on rural workforce recruitment and stabilization. The initiative also aligns with the state's existing Graduate Medical Education (GME) and Statewide Healthcare Access and Recruitment Program (SHARP) for a unified, data-driven workforce pipeline. Multiple RFAs and opportunities are open or pending for rural-focused workforce projects and sub-programs.

data.title: IA - 2026 - Best and Brightest- Medical Equipment Procurement
data.highlights: Iowa HHS issued a Notice of Intent to Award for a $66M CMS/HHS-funded medical equipment procurement for numerous rural hospitals statewide. Awards are not final until contracts are executed. This funding will modernize hospital equipment throughout rural Iowa.

data.title: IA - 2026 - Best and Brightest- Medical Equipment Procurement (9a3bb8)
data.highlights: The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services has issued a Notice of Intent to Award for the Best and Brightest- Medical Equipment Procurement program, supported entirely by CMS/HHS with a total funding of approximately $66 million. Multiple Iowa rural hospitals and health centers are named as apparent successful bidders pending contract execution. The procurement will enhance rural medical equipment infrastructure across the state.

data.title: IA - 2026 - Best and Brightest – Rural Healthcare Workforce Recruitment
data.highlights: The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services intends to award a CMS-funded workforce recruitment contract totaling $12.6M for rural hospitals and providers across Iowa. Over 70 rural hospitals and clinics are named as recipients, primarily for physician, nursing, and advanced practice recruitment. All funds are federally sourced, with no required state match.

data.title: IA - 2025 - RHTP – Healthy Hometowns
data.highlights: This application outlines Iowa's strategy to leverage the Rural Health Transformation Program for significant improvements in rural health care. Key initiatives include care coordination, specialty access, workforce recruitment, cancer prevention and treatment, telehealth investments, health information exchange expansion, and EMS innovation. The plan targets measurable improvements in access, local service availability, care coordination, and rural health outcomes.

data.title: IA - 2025 - Iowa RHTP (Healthy Hometowns)
data.highlights: Iowa's application sets forth an ambitious, five-year transformation plan emphasizing a hub-and-spoke care model, population health, technology, health information exchange, and strategic rural partnerships. Major initiatives include Hometown Connections, EMS Community Care Mobile, Communities of Care, and Combat Cancer: Prevent and Treat. The strategy addresses rural infrastructure, workforce gaps, access barriers, and chronic disease through innovative and evidence-based approaches.

data.title: GA - 2024 - Georgia RHTP (includes GA-STRONG, GA-AIDE, Medicaid DPPs)
data.highlights: This document aggregates advocacy input, statewide strategy recommendations, and program design feedback related to Georgia's use of Medicaid-directed funding (DPPs, including GA-STRONG and GA-AIDE) to expand and sustain rural health access. Topics include rural and youth mental health crisis, inclusion parity for pediatric hospitals, maternal/OB workforce shortages, and the urgent need to stabilize and grow Georgia's rural health workforce through targeted Medicaid funding approaches.

data.title: GA - 2026 - Georgia Medicaid Directed Payment Programs
data.highlights: Georgia's Medicaid DPP for SFY 2026 provides $4.3 billion in advanced payments across eight programs targeting rural hospitals, maternal health, workforce shortages, and quality improvement. New payment structures stabilize rural OB units and expand provider access. All payments are CMS-approved and tied to Medicaid Managed Care utilization and quality targets.

data.title: GA - 2025 - Rural Hospital Tax Credit Program
data.highlights: This operations manual sets forth the procedures for the Rural Hospital Tax Credit Program in Georgia for calendar years 2025-2026. It includes instructions, timelines, ranking methodology for financial need, and requirements for hospital submissions to support financial viability efforts in rural hospitals.

data.title: GA - 2025 - Tax Credit Donations Five-Year Plan
data.highlights: This document provides guidance for rural hospitals to submit a five-year plan focused on using tax credit donations to address debt, uncompensated care, and financial viability challenges. It emphasizes financial strategies to ensure long-term stability.

data.title: GA - 2026 - Rural Hospital Tax Credit - 2026 Ranking of Financial Need
data.highlights: This document provides a ranked listing of rural hospitals in Georgia according to financial need for the 2026 Rural Hospital Tax Credit program. It is intended to guide financial assistance targeting.

data.title: GA - 2026 - Rural Hospital Tax Credit Program
data.highlights: Document lists rural hospital organizations preliminarily eligible for the Rural Hospital Tax Credit Program for calendar year 2026. Eligibility requires submission of annual documentation to the Department of Community Health.

data.title: GA - 2026 - Georgia Rural Enhancement And Transformation of Health (GREAT Health) Program
data.highlights: Georgia's GREAT Health RHTP strategy comprises five initiatives aligned with CMS AHEAD model goals, including sustainable health systems, access, workforce, and technology innovations. The strategy describes hospital global budget models, primary care transformation, milestones for rural hospitals, EMR technology upgrades, and engagement via advisory councils. Detailed timelines and milestone activities are planned for 2026-2031, with stakeholder partnerships across state agencies and hospital entities.

data.title: PA - 2026 - RHTP Public Webinar, March 31, 2026
data.highlights:
The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania is hosting a series of Regional Rural Health Summits throughout 2025-2026 to identify region-specific challenges and develop action plans for rural health transformation. The March 31, 2026 public webinar introduced the structure and first-year plans for the Rural Health Transformation Program, emphasizing stakeholder involvement and regional collaboration. Key focus areas include improving healthcare access, building local workforce pipelines, and supporting long-term economic growth.

data.title: US - 2025 - Rural Healthcare Capital Funding Analysis
data.highlights: This policy paper analyzes capital access challenges facing rural hospitals and other rural health facilities. It presents an overview of major capital funding programs and historical trends, emphasizing the complexity of blended financing and persistent access barriers. The report highlights the importance of technical assistance, partnerships, and varied funding streams for sustaining and modernizing rural healthcare infrastructure.

data.title: FL - 2024 - EMS Supplement Workplan Activities
data.highlights: This plan outlines yearly recurring recruitment and retention activities for EMS providers through FY2028. It tracks outcomes like workforce composition, billing practices, and job satisfaction at the agency level, supporting workforce and system capacity in rural EMS. Goals and measures are monitored annually.

data.title: FL - 2024 - Flex Program
data.highlights: This document provides states participating in Flex Year 4 with guidance and examples for incorporating outcome measures into rural health programs. It describes both Quality Improvement and Financial/Operational Improvement outcome frameworks and provides example activities and benchmarks for each. The guidance encourages moving beyond process measures to demonstrate meaningful impact on CAH quality and financial outcomes.

data.title: NY - 2025 - RHTP – Application & Process 1/16/2026| 1
data.highlights: New York was awarded $212 million under the Rural Health Transformation Program for 2025-2030 to implement a highly collaborative set of rural health strategies across 47 rural counties. Key focus areas include healthcare workforce development, health IT and cybersecurity, access to care via Patient Centered Medical Homes, and building comprehensive rural health partnerships. NY’s plan was developed with stakeholder and community input and aims for scalable, sustainable rural healthcare improvement.

data.title: NY - 2025 - New York State RHTP
data.highlights: New York's RHTP application identifies persistent disparities in health access and outcomes across its 2.1 million rural residents, with concerted strategies targeting workforce gaps, service closures, technology access, and financial instability. The plan proposes multi-level initiatives focused on developing collaborative health care networks, advancing primary care and behavioral health integration, modernizing rural health IT infrastructure, and growing a sustainable workforce pipeline. Strategic investments, robust partnerships, and data-driven planning anchor the state's approach to rural health system transformation.

data.title: NY - 2026 - New York State RHT Plan
data.highlights: New York aims to transform rural health through four key initiatives focusing on care coordination, technology-enhanced primary care, workforce development, and technology innovation including telehealth and cybersecurity. The program is informed by extensive stakeholder engagement and prioritizes funding to areas of highest rural need.

data.title: OH - 2025 - Ohio Informational Call Thursday, Sept. 18 And Thursday, Sept. 25, 2025 RHTP Slide Deck
data.highlights: The document provides information on Ohio's Rural Health Transformation Program for fiscal year 2025, including call objectives, strategic goals, federal guidance criteria, and a timeline for statewide stakeholder engagement and federal award deadlines. It serves as an informational and guidance resource for stakeholders preparing for the RHTP application.

data.title: OH - 2025 - Ohio RHTP
data.highlights: This is Ohio's multi-year plan for the Rural Health Transformation Program, focused on improving access, outcomes, and sustainability for rural hospitals and Medicaid beneficiaries. The plan proposes clinically integrated networks, school-based health, expanded EMS and pharmacy services, workforces pipelines, and value-based Medicaid reforms. Priorities include addressing chronic disease, maternal/infant mortality, behavioral health, and persistent rural disparities in provider supply and health outcomes.

data.title: OH - 2025 - Ohio RHTP (Rural+Health+Transformation+Letter)
data.highlights: This is Ohio's official application for the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program, outlining comprehensive statewide strategies to improve rural health. The proposal includes expanding school-based health centers, investing in workforce development, telehealth, EMS upgrades, integrated care, and social determinants like nutrition and physical fitness. Key priorities focus on chronic disease, infant mortality, vision care, technology adoption, and improved local capacity.

data.title: OH - 2025 - RHTP - Ohio Application
data.highlights: Ohio's proposal seeks RHTP funding to expand proven and innovative health models for rural communities, including workforce development, technology-enabled care, and improved EMS. The application emphasizes partnerships, expanded school-based and home visiting programs, and leverages data-driven accountability. Policy reforms targeting SNAP nutrition, licensure compacts, and pharmacy practice aim to support sustained rural transformation.

data.title: NH - 2026 - RHT Fund (RHTF)
data.highlights: This document is a summary and preparatory overview for New Hampshire's potential participation in the federal Rural Health Transformation Fund (RHTF), planning to invest an anticipated $500 million over five years if awarded. It outlines application requirements, potential investments, and stakeholder engagement milestones under CMS guidance. The state is preparing its application with an emphasis on workforce, partnerships, technology, and enduring rural health transformation.

NH - 2025 - RHTP - New Hampshire
data.highlights: This strategic plan outlines New Hampshire's ambitious approach for rural health transformation under RHTP. data.title: MI - 2025 - Michigan Medicaid; Healthy Michigan Plan
data.highlights: This executive and fiscal analysis by the State of Michigan details the potential impact of proposed major federal Medicaid cuts, including risks to coverage for over 2.6 million Michiganders, particularly in rural communities. It outlines effects on the rural hospital system, state budget, uncompensated care, employment, and critical health services. Report highlights the Medicaid program's cost-effectiveness and vital support for Michigan's rural and safety net healthcare infrastructure.

data.title: MI - 2025 - RHTP Proposal Michigan
data.highlights: This is Michigan's CMS Rural Health Transformation Program application outlining a statewide plan to transform rural health care systems. The proposed strategy includes four major initiatives: cross-sector partnership hubs, rural workforce development, advancing health IT interoperability, and bringing care closer to home via innovative models. A dedicated 5% resource carve-out supports tribal governments’ health system capacity.

data.title: CO - 2025 - Healthy Colorado For All / Hospital Transformation Program
data.highlights: Colorado’s 2025-26 Healthy Colorado For All report showcases implementation milestones in immunizations, maternity, behavioral health, and prevention, emphasizing health equity and regional variation. Rural disparities remain pronounced, with 11% of Medicaid members in rural and 3% in frontier counties, half of rural areas classified as Maternity Care Deserts, and persistent differences in diabetes control and oral health by race/ethnicity. Major reforms include ACC Phase III launch, Medicaid eConsult platform, expanded doula services, and the approved HRSN (1115) waiver for broader social supports.

data.title: CO - 2025 - Colorado Department of Health Care Policy & Financing Performance Plan
data.highlights: Colorado HCPF is launching the ACC Phase III with more rural hospital and provider support, advanced value-based care, and targeted population health strategies. Major goals include controlling Medicaid cost trends, increasing automation in member renewals, expanding provider networks (especially for behavioral health and prenatal care), and protecting rural health system viability. The plan targets improved access and outcomes for rural, aging, and at-risk populations while navigating federal Medicaid changes.

data.title: CO - 2026 - Colorado Medicaid Work Requirements Implementation APD (in response to H.R.1)
data.highlights: Colorado will implement multi-year, phased system upgrades to Medicaid technology platforms to meet new federal work requirements by January 1, 2027, prioritizing timely compliance and coverage continuity for eligible members. State plans include advanced data sharing, automation, verification systems, and robust project management, with significant roles for public-private and multi-agency partnerships. Over $54 million in federal and state funding supports the initiative, with a 90/10 federal match for system DDI and related enhancements.

data.title: FL - 2026 - rural health (d4ff24)
data.highlights: The program supports small rural hospitals via Medicare Rural Hospital Flexibility (Flex) and Small Rural Hospital Improvement Program (SHIP) funding to improve quality and transition to value-based care. It also enhances rural EMS training and coordinates activities with rural health networks and local health councils across the state.

data.highlights: The Colorado RHTP Advisory Committee kicked off oversight of a major federal investment of $200M+ to support rural health transformation, supported 100% by CMS/HHS. The program involves extensive planning, stakeholder input, charter/rules development, and will fund subgrantee initiatives via competitive RFAs with a focus on sustainability, workforce, quality, and health system redesign. data.title: CO - 2025 - Colorado First Colorado RHTP Advisory Committee meeting

data.title: CO - 2026 - RHTP Advisory Committee Meeting

data.title: CO - 2026 - Colorado RHTP: Project Summary
data.highlights: Colorado's RHTP aims to support rural hospitals, clinics, and communities through investment in telehealth, workforce recruitment, and partnership-building to advance sustainable rural health care. The program prioritizes keeping care local while modernizing delivery and improving access to essential services.

data.title: VT - 2026 - Vermont RHTP
data.highlights: Vermont's application details an ambitious transformation of rural health care through 30 proposed initiatives and grant programs targeting regionalization, integrated shared service platforms, stronger primary care, and major investments in rural provider and workforce development. The state will fund both service delivery reforms and physical facility and IT modernization, emphasizing EMS/paramedicine, mobile units, analytics, telehealth, housing, workforce pipelines, and more. data.title: WA - 2026 - Washington RHTP An Overview Summary

data.title: WA - 2026 - Project Narrative RHTP

data.title: VT - 2024 - States Advancing All-Payer Health Equity Approaches and Development (AHEAD) Model (2024.12.16_Draft_Vermont_AHEAD_State_Agreement_for_website)

data.title: VT - 2024 - States Advancing All-Payer Health Equity Approaches and Development (AHEAD) Model

data.title: MS - 2024 - Mississippi Medicaid State Directed Payment Arrangement (Uniform Dollar Increase 2024-2025)

data.title: OR - 2026 - Oregon RHT Plan

data.title: OR - 2025 - 10-16-25 RHTP Public Survey Results 1
data.highlights: More than 400 public responses shaped OHA's RHTP application strategy. Community priorities emphasized workforce capacity, prevention, behavioral health, and technology modernization, with strong support for investments in CHWs and rural training pipelines. Regional partnerships and HIT infrastructure considered essential for long-term transformation, though technology modernization was seen as less immediately impactful.

data.title: OR - 2026 - 10.9.2025 RHTP Public Forum
data.highlights: Oregon’s RHTP strategy aligns with CMS strategic goals to promote innovation, workforce, access, and technology for rural health transformation. $100 million federal annual allocation is projected if awarded, supporting a portfolio of initiatives in prevention, workforce, technology, partnerships, and systems. Public comment and ongoing tribal consultation are shaping priorities, with strong focus on regional tailoring, immediate impact and sustainability, and addressing critical access, workforce, technology, behavioral health, and maternal health needs.

data.title: OR - 2026 - 12.2.2025 RHTP
data.highlights: Oregon's RHTP aims to transform rural health infrastructure and services through a five-year plan supported by an estimated $100 million annually in federal funding. Strategic initiatives focus on strengthening regional partnerships, supporting rural hospitals and clinics, modernizing health IT, boosting workforce capacity, and targeting maternal, behavioral, and chronic disease health priorities. The plan emphasizes both immediate-impact projects and long-term sustainable reforms, with explicit attention to frontier and Tribal communities.

data.title: NJ - 2026 - rural health
data.highlights: New Jersey has applied for major federal funding through the new RHTP, a $50 billion national initiative. Input from healthcare providers and community organizations has helped the state identify priorities, gaps, and opportunities for rural health care improvement. The program emphasizes information exchange, workforce recruitment, community engagement, and strong partnerships. Key contacts: Hannah Schonman NJST.Ruralhealth@doh.nj.gov

data.title: MS - 2022 - Mississippi Division of Medicaid Health Information Network (HIN)
data.highlights: Multiple Mississippi hospitals are attesting to collaborate and participate in a statewide Health Information Network for Medicaid data reporting. The HIN initiative is intended to improve admission, discharge, and transfer data exchange for Medicaid beneficiaries, as a requirement in the SFY 2022 plan. The document serves to certify hospitals' capability and intent to support statewide HIN implementation.

data.title: MD - 2025 - Maryland RHTP
data.highlights: Maryland recognizes 18 of its 24 jurisdictions as rural, and 25% of Marylanders live in these areas. The Maryland State Office of Rural Health leads strategic initiatives coordinating programming, providing technical assistance, and disseminating rural health best practices. Current strategic planning focuses on workforce development, chronic disease, and access to care in rural regions.

data.title: LA - 2025 - Louisiana RHTP (LA RHTP)
data.highlights: Louisiana submits a robust Rural Health Transformation Program (LA RHTP) application to CMS to comprehensively transform rural health systems for Louisiana’s 1.1 million rural residents. The strategy centers on workforce expansion, digital modernization (including a statewide shared CMS-certified EHR), innovative payment reform, community collaboration, and targeted population health efforts for chronic disease, maternal health, behavioral, and cancer priorities. The plan details proposed investments of $485M over five years for workforce, technology, care delivery, and financial stabilization.

data.title: LA - 2025 - Louisiana RHTP
data.highlights: Louisiana is preparing an application for the federal Rural Health Transformation Program, which allocates approximately $200 million per year over five years to the state for rural health infrastructure, workforce, and access. The strategy focuses on high-morbidity, provider shortage areas and emphasizes innovative care models, strategic partnerships, and improving health outcomes. Rural health priorities include heart disease, diabetes, obesity, and tobacco use, all at higher rates than urban areas.

data.title: LA - 2027 - Louisiana Department of Health - RHTP Overview
data.highlights:
Louisiana will receive over $208 million through the Rural Health Transformation Program, one of the highest awards in the nation and top three in the Southeast. The program supports rural health transformation and Medicaid in Louisiana.

The Office of Rural Health also works with rural health networks and local health councils to coordinate statewide rural health efforts.

data.title: AZ - 2022 - Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS) Health IT Strategy
data.highlights: This document is Arizona's 2022-2026 Health IT Strategy, providing a framework to guide statewide health IT investments and strategy after the HITECH Act. It emphasizes health information exchange (HIE), collaboration among payers and providers, and addresses population health, equity, and modernization. Rural health challenges, provider shortages, and disparities among racial/ethnic groups are central, with solutions focused on interoperability and leveraging partnerships.

data.title: CA - 2025 - Small and Rural Hospital Relief Program
data.highlights: This document sets the 2025 California regulatory standards for seismic safety in hospital buildings, with significant attention to rural, small, and financially distressed hospitals. The Small and Rural Hospital Relief Program, administered by HCAI, includes targeted seismic safety grant opportunities intended to prevent hospital closures in vulnerable rural communities. Deadlines for seismic safety compliance, financial hardship criteria, and extension provisions are newly defined for 2025 and beyond.

data.title: CA - 2023 - Small and Rural Hospital Relief Program (SRHRP)
data.highlights: California’s Small and Rural Hospital Relief Program (SRHRP) provides state grant funding and technical assistance for seismic compliance to small, rural, and Critical Access Hospitals. The program is supported by excise tax revenue on electronic cigarettes and a 2023-24 budget allocation. Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis, and eligible projects include both planning/design and construction activities related to seismic resistance.

data.title: CA - 2026 - California RHT (CA-RHT)
data.highlights: The CA-RHT program will launch three major, interconnected initiatives to expand care access, modernize infrastructure, and stabilize and grow the rural health workforce. Over $233 million in federal funds are proposed for investment in California rural health, with $35 million targeted specifically to stabilize strategically important rural hospitals. A strong commitment to Tribal health equity and modernization of health IT infrastructure is central to the plan.

data.title: CA - 2026 - California RHT (CA-RHT) (Project-Narrative-RHTP-v3-2026-03-27)
data.highlights: California's Rural Health Transformation Plan (CA-RHT) proposes a statewide hub-and-spoke model to improve rural hospital viability, workforce capacity, digital health infrastructure, and access to primary, maternity, specialty, and behavioral health care. A minimum of 5% of the program's funds is dedicated to Tribal clinic participation. The plan emphasizes value-based payment innovation, technology integration such as telehealth and health information exchange, and regionally coordinated networks to close rural access and outcomes gaps.

data.title: CA - 2026 - Frequently Asked Questions
data.highlights:
This document outlines key frequently asked questions for applicants and stakeholders regarding California's CalRHT program. It addresses eligibility, funding, application timelines, and priority populations, including required allocations for Tribal communities. CalRHT will use a hub-and-spoke network model to support rural transformation and will engage stakeholders through RHPC and regular communications. Key contacts: CalRHT@hcai.ca.gov

data.highlights:
The California Rural Health Transformation (CalRHT) program is the state's implementation of the federal Rural Health Transformation Program, aiming to improve health care delivery in rural communities. The program is administered by the Department of Health Care Access and Information and focuses on tackling workforce shortages, access challenges, and infrastructure barriers specific to rural California. No specific hospital or provider awards are announced in this document.

data.title: AZ - 2025 - Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System (AHCCCS) Medicaid Program
data.highlights: The AHCCCS 2025-2029 Strategic Plan emphasizes advancing whole-person care, reducing the uninsured rate, and improving provider satisfaction. Notable initiatives include the H2O program to connect housing and health resources and a modernization of the Medicaid Enterprise System to strengthen fraud, waste, and abuse oversight. Stakeholder engagement and data-driven targeting underpin efforts to enhance health outcomes for rural and Medicaid populations.

data.title: AZ - 2025 - Arizona RHTP (Arizona'sRHTP_ProgramWhitePaper)
data.highlights: Arizona was awarded $166,988,956 in federal funds under RHTP to strengthen rural healthcare. Strategic focus areas include telehealth expansion, workforce development, EHR upgrades, and grants for behavioral health, chronic disease, and maternal health. The program phases include setup, implementation, and continuous improvement with ongoing stakeholder engagement.

data.title: AZ - 2025 - RHTP Post-Submission Public Webinar Originally Presented: November 13, 2025 Revised to Reflect Official CMS Funding Allocation: March 12, 2026
data.highlights: Arizona was awarded $166 million for Year 1 of the Rural Health Transformation Program, the largest federal rural health innovation investment in state history. Major initiatives include workforce expansion, behavioral health, telehealth modernization, maternal health, and chronic disease prevention, with sub-awards allocated to targeted programs. Extensive stakeholder engagement shaped Arizona's application and ongoing governance structure.

data.title: AZ - 2025 - Accessing Behavioral Health Services in Schools
data.highlights: The AHCCCS, in partnership with the Arizona Department of Education, provides guidance for accessing behavioral health services in schools, streamlines referrals to community providers, and offers suicide prevention training for all school staff. Efforts prioritize Medicaid-enrolled and underinsured students, aiming to remove barriers to care and improve rural health outcomes. Multiple grants and resources are coordinated statewide to support behavioral health and substance use treatment access.

data.title: AZ - 2025 - Arizona RHTP (Initiatives)
data.highlights: Arizona's Rural Health Transformation Program is a $167 million, five-year effort managed by AHCCCS to strengthen rural healthcare access and workforce. Major investments include workforce development, priority health initiatives, expanded care access, and support for rural hospitals and clinics. The initiative aims to directly benefit more than 786,000 Arizonans living in rural communities.

data.title: VT - 2025 - Vermont Statewide Health Care Delivery Transformation & Payment Reform
data.highlights: Act No. 68 (2025) directs Vermont to structurally transform healthcare payment, delivery, and hospital regulation, centering on global hospital budgets and reference-based pricing as well as a robust accountability structure. The state will develop and periodically update a comprehensive Health Care Delivery Strategic Plan, involving both rural and urban hospitals, stakeholders, and multi-agency oversight. Emphasis is placed on primary care, rural provider stabilization, data integration, and cost containment.

data.title: VT - 2025 - Vermont Health Care Payment and Delivery System Reform (S.126; Statewide Health Care Delivery Strategic Plan)
data.highlights: This act mandates broad reforms to Vermont’s health care payment and delivery systems, including new statewide oversight and restructuring of hospital budgeting, rate-setting, and financial transparency. Initiatives include implementation of reference-based pricing, strategic investment in workforce and primary care, the establishment of a comprehensive, multi-agency, data-driven Statewide Health Care Delivery Strategic Plan, and mechanisms to ensure sustainable access to essential services—especially in rural and underserved areas. Progress is tied to defined milestones with required stakeholder input, annual benchmarking, and future updates as policy evolves.

data.title: VT - 2026 - CMS-RHT-26-001 RHTP Application Submission from the State of Vermont
data.highlights:
Vermont’s RHT plan is a comprehensive, data-driven strategy aimed at strengthening rural health care workforce, improving timely access to care, and reducing costs through regionalization, coordinated planning, technology investments, and innovative care strategies. The application details the state’s rural health needs, with focused interventions in high-need rural counties and clear statewide performance targets. The plan addresses persistent gaps in workforce, infrastructure, chronic disease, mental health, access, and financial stability for rural hospitals. Key contacts: Linda Blasch Linda.Blasch@vermont.gov; DVHA (Department of Vermont Health Access); AHS (Agency of Human Services); DFR (Department of Financial Regulation)

data.title: WV - 2026 - West Virginia Secures $199 Million in 2026 from Rural Healthcare Transformation Fund

data.title: WI - 2024 - Obstetric Delivery Services and Workforce in Rural Wisconsin Hospitals 2024
data.highlights: This report updates trends in hospital-based obstetric delivery services and workforce in rural Wisconsin, following declines in rural births and increased unit closures. Innovative practices, like the rural OB-GYN residency at UW-Madison and sustainable models at Hayward and Monroe, are highlighted as actionable solutions. Recommendations are targeted to policymakers and hospitals, emphasizing Medicaid expansion and reimbursement, rural workforce development, use of residency and fellowship programs, and promotion of telehealth and non-traditional care models. Key contacts: Penny Black pdblack@wisc.edu

data.title: WI - 2025 - Critical Access Hospitals: Meeting Rural Community Needs! — Wisconsin Office of Rural Health review of CHNAs and CHIPs
data.highlights:
This Wisconsin Office of Rural Health report summarizes the top community health priorities as identified by the state's Critical Access Hospitals from recent Community Health Needs Assessments and Improvement Plans. Mental health and substance abuse are consistently rated as top concerns, with many hospitals also committed to addressing chronic disease, social drivers of health, and access barriers. The findings support statewide alignment and shared learning to advance rural health transformation.

data.highlights:
WI-DHS is implementing RHTP in partnership with 16 state agencies and over 29 projects. A dedicated External Advisory Council, with regional representation, meets quarterly to provide feedback and recommendations. The program is proceeding according to schedule, with most implementation partners having begun work and detailed plans. Key contacts: John Eich info@worh.org

data.title: WA - 2026 - In a crisis? Free or low-cost health care
data.highlights:
Washington received approximately $181 million from CMS in the first year of the program to support rural hospitals, clinics, and providers. The program is administered by a partnership between the Health Care Authority, Department of Health, Department of Social and Health Services, and the Governor's Office. Recent program extensions and funding opportunities focus on maternal, emergency, specialty services, provider technology, and opioid treatment workforce support.

data.title: US - 2026 - Federal Reporting And Rescoring Webinar February 25, 2026 RHTP
data.highlights: This draft CMS webinar provides detailed guidance on RHT Program state-level annual and quarterly reporting requirements. It outlines program timelines, required templates, the rescoring process for funding decisions, and the shift from Excel to a web-based reporting tool for states. No specific state- or initiative-level data is included, as this is a general federal instructional document.

data.title: US - 2026 - Federal Category B Funding For Provider Payments RHTP Summary
data.highlights: This fact sheet provides guidance on allowable and unallowable uses of Category B Provider Payments under the Rural Health Transformation Program. It outlines restrictions, sustainability requirements, and the 15% cap on Category B funding, as well as allowable example expenditures tied to state RHT transformation plan initiatives. The document clarifies payment models and directs states to ensure RHTP funds do not duplicate existing programs.

data.title: US - 2026 - CMS RHTP
data.highlights: This document announces the FY2026 federal grant allocations for all 50 states under the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program, created by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Each state's RHTP award, totaling $10 billion across the US, supports rural health transformation initiatives spanning workforce, technology, population health, payment reform, and rural Medicaid.

data.title: US - 2025 - RHT Program State Project Abstracts
data.highlights: This document compiles State-level abstracts from Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) applications submitted in December 2025. Each abstract summarizes the purpose, anticipated outcomes, major partners, and proposed program activities to be implemented with RHTP funds under the federal initiative. The document presents illustrative budgets, details of transformation plans, and a wide array of strategic approaches but is intended for public information and does not reflect final awards.

data.title: US - 2026 - RHTP Engagement Events in August
data.highlights:
The program provides $50 billion in funding over five fiscal years from 2026 to 2030 to approved states, supporting initiatives such as evidence-based interventions, workforce development, technology adoption, and innovative care models. Funds are allocated equally and on a needs basis considering rural population and facility characteristics. States must use funds for at least three approved uses including improving prevention, supporting workforce retention, promoting technology-driven solutions, and advancing sustainable access.

data.title: UT - 2025 - Section 1115 Demonstration Authority for Workforce Initiatives
data.highlights: CMS issued guidance stating it will not approve or extend new section 1115 demonstration authorities for workforce initiatives beyond currently approved projects. Five workforce demonstration projects have been previously approved involving over $1 billion in federal commitments.

data.title: UT - 2026 - Utah RHTP
data.highlights: Utah received a $195.7 million federal RHTP award for 2026, with initiatives spanning preventive health, rural workforce, infrastructure, technology, and innovation. 25 of Utah’s 29 counties are rural. Year 1 program initiatives are clearly defined, with multiple partners and a focus on competitive sub-awards for remaining funds.

keyDates.label: Budget revision and progress report due

data.title: VA - 2025 - Cardinal Care Managed Care (CCMC)
data.highlights: Virginia is re-procuring its statewide Medicaid managed care program, Cardinal Care Managed Care, with enhanced focus on quality improvement, data-driven analytics, and equitable access to care. The program introduces a single managed care contract, new models and value-based care initiatives, and specialized plans for foster care youth. Transition to new MCOs and enrollment enhancements take effect July 1, 2025.

data.title: TN - 2023 - Tennessee Rural Health Care Task Force
data.highlights: This 2023 Task Force report offers actionable recommendations to improve rural access to care, workforce development, and social drivers of health in Tennessee. Strategic initiatives include a Center of Excellence, care access and telehealth pilots, expanded apprenticeship and training programs, and support for county health councils through grants and partnerships. Recommendations emphasize leveraging both public and private resources.

data.title: TN - 2023 - Tennessee Rural Health Care Task Force Initiative
data.highlights: This report outlines the findings and recommendations developed by the Tennessee Rural Health Care Task Force during its 2022-2023 term. It presents a comprehensive strategic vision and budget proposals to improve rural access to care, transform the health care workforce, address social drivers of health, and sustain rural hospitals. The recommendations include establishing a Center of Excellence, new funding models, workforce pathways, and telemedicine investments.

data.title: VA - 2025 - Virginia Medicaid Transformation / Cardinal Care Managed Care
data.highlights: In 2025, Virginia launched its largest-ever Medicaid managed care transformation, transitioning 1.7 million people into the Cardinal Care system. Major advances include improved outcomes in maternal and behavioral health, significant reductions in avoidable emergency room visits, and strengthened oversight mechanisms. The state reported robust workforce retention, enhanced IT security, and progress in language and disability access.

data.title: TN - 2025 - See Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee's Announcement of Tennessee's Proposal
data.highlights: Tennessee has submitted its application for the federal Rural Health Transformation Program, aiming to invest in rural healthcare improvements including facility modernization, maternal and child health, prevention, health technology, and workforce development. The proposal builds on prior state progress such as task forces, resiliency programs, and health centers of excellence.

data.title: VA - 2025 - VA Rural Vitality (rhc-transformation-project-narrative)
data.highlights: The Commonwealth of Virginia seeks significant rural healthcare transformation through the VA Rural Vitality application, focusing on four strategic initiatives (CareIQ, Homegrown Health Heroes, Connected Care Closer to Home, Live Well Together). The approach targets chronic disease, maternal and infant health, mental health, access, workforce, and provider solvency using technology, workforce pipelines, and community partnerships. Rural residents face disparities across all health indicators, with program structure responding to direct stakeholder feedback from broad rural engagement.

data.title: TN - 2025 - RHTP Application Opportunity Number: CMS-RHT-26-001 Project Narrative Submitted by the State of Tennessee Tennessee Department of Health November 5, 2025
data.highlights: This application proposes a comprehensive $125 million investment in rural health transformation across Tennessee, with a focus on access, workforce, technology, and prevention. Major strategies include competitive grants for facility upgrades, EMS and mobile health expansions, primary/dental care access for the uninsured, workforce training pipelines, and sweeping policy modernization. Rural Tennessee's health challenges—chronic disease, maternal mortality, provider shortages, hospital financial distress—are directly targeted through coordinated initiatives and statewide collaboration.

data.title: VA - 2026 - Virginia RHT Initiative Overview
data.highlights:
Virginia is advancing the Rural Health Transformation initiative by assessing local needs, sharing best practices, and deploying innovative solutions to improve rural healthcare access and quality. The Department of Medical Assistance Services highlights improvements in postpartum care and crisis response impacting over two million Virginians.

data.title: VA - 2026 - The Rural Health Care Transformation initiative is a statewide effort to strengthen health care in Virginia’s rural communities.
data.highlights: The program was developed through extensive stakeholder engagement including 12 listening sessions and input from over 200 organizations, resulting in four key goals to improve access, outcomes, and innovation. The initiative brings together state and local agencies, providers, nonprofits, business partners, and community stakeholders. Virginia submitted a detailed application to CMS to secure federal funding for expanding access, growing the workforce, and driving innovation in rural areas.

data.title: TN - 2026 - Tennessee RHTP
data.highlights: The Tennessee Rural Health Transformation Program was awarded $206.9 million by CMS for its first five-year budget period with the goal of advancing rural health sustainability, innovation, technology, maternal/child health, and workforce solutions. Anticipated upcoming grant opportunities (RFPs) span a variety of objectives, including health resiliency, community-based prevention, and workforce development, and will open starting in 2026. The document provides programmatic guidance, outlines strategic pillars, and details future application processes.

data.title: TX - 2022 - RH-CHRG Tier 1 Direct Award
data.highlights: This report is required from every Texas rural hospital that received a $250,000 direct award under the Tier 1 RH-CHRG program. Funds could be used for staffing, telemedicine, equipment, PPE, and other eligible expenses. Grantees must document expenditure and submit the report by the specified deadline to avoid recoupment.

data.title: TX - 2024 - Medicaid Managed Care Aligning Technology by Linking Interoperable Systems (ATLIS) for Client Health Outcomes Program
data.highlights: This guidance document establishes performance milestones and bi-annual reporting processes for the ATLIS Program, advancing statewide connectivity and health information exchange for Medicaid managed care. Incentive arrangements are structured to reward MCOs for achieving progress in digital data exchange and improving client outcomes. Year 1 focuses on assessing existing hospital and MCO connectivity and interoperability, with additional measures to track future improvements.

data.title: TX - 2025 - ATLIS Incentive Payments for Medicaid Managed Care Organizations
data.highlights: This document provides incentive pool percentage allocations and estimated potential payments by managed care organization and region for state fiscal year 2025. The ATLIS program incentivizes Medicaid MCOs to achieve benchmarks in service delivery areas, with payments tied to rural hospital care and Medicaid populations. Recipients and amounts are estimated and contingent on actual capitation payments.

data.title: TX - 2026 - RHTP (RHT) / Rural Texas Strong
data.highlights: Texas HHSC was awarded $281.3 million from CMS for the first year of the Rural Health Transformation Program. The funding will launch the Rural Texas Strong program and six major rural health initiatives, pending final budget approval and allocation processes. Sub-award and eligibility processes have not yet begun.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Rural Texas Strong (RHTP)
data.highlights: Texas is awarded $1.4 billion over five years for the Rural Texas Strong program under the federal Rural Health Transformation Program. Six major initiatives will address prevention/wellness, health IT, telehealth, workforce, cybersecurity, and infrastructure for rural healthcare providers. Implementation activities will run from 2026 through 2031, with funds distributed to rural health entities statewide through various procurement and grant processes.

data.title: TX - 2025 - Rural Texas Strong
data.highlights: The Rural Texas Strong project is a comprehensive, statewide RHTP application to transform rural health care for all rural Texans, prioritizing local implementation and sustainability. The strategy addresses chronic disease, maternal health, workforce and technology challenges with innovative, data-driven, and locally focused solutions. Texas targets measurable outcomes involving patient access, provider infrastructure, technology, workforce pipeline, and hospital financial health by 2031.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Rural Texas Strong Program (RHTP)
data.highlights: Texas received $281.3 million for Budget Period 1 for the Rural Health Transformation Program, an increase from its original proposal. The program funds direct and competitive subawards via six major initiatives aligned with CMS guidance, with significant allocations for rural hospital implementation, workforce, behavioral health, and EMS infrastructure. The implementation approach emphasizes timely obligation and liquidation of funds to maximize early impact and meet federal requirements.

data.title: TX - 2025 - Rural Texas Strong (CMS RHT-26-001)
data.highlights: Texas has developed the Rural Texas Strong statewide transformation plan to serve 202 rural counties, prioritizing technological innovation, direct funding to local rural health systems, and workforce development. Target populations include 3.7 million rural residents and 155 rural hospitals, with evidence-based initiatives to address chronic disease, workforce shortages, and infrastructure gaps. The plan sets specific performance metrics and strategic goals to address access, technology, partnerships, workforce sustainability, and rural provider solvency.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Texas RHTP
data.highlights: Texas HHSC was awarded $281,319,361 in Year 1 as part of a five-year RHTP plan totaling over $1.4 billion. 80 rural hospital districts will receive direct awards to strengthen rural healthcare delivery, while key investments are made in workforce, EMS capacity, and health data infrastructure. Project includes substantial investment in AMBUS mobile units for emergency response and large operational support for rural health workforce training and capital improvements.

data.title: TX - 2025 - Rural Texas Strong (rural-txstrong-accessible-prjct-narr-supp-materials)
data.highlights: The Rural Texas Strong project is a statewide CMS RHTP application designed to address the significant rural health challenges in Texas, with innovative initiatives in workforce, technology, chronic disease, financial solvency, and access. It targets over 3.7 million rural residents across 202 rural counties, prioritizing prevention, wellness, chronic disease management, and infrastructure modernization. Performance targets for 2031 aim to improve provider ratios, remote monitoring, telehealth, health IT, and rural hospital financial metrics.

data.title: TX - 2025 - One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) RHTP – Rural Texas Strong
data.highlights: This is the Texas state application for the Rural Health Transformation Program under the OBBBA Act, known as Rural Texas Strong. It outlines a strategic, multi-initiative plan spanning 2025-2030 to transform rural healthcare through local investments, partnerships, and infrastructure upgrades. Major areas of focus include expanding rural workforce, telehealth and health IT, supporting rural-urban clinical partnerships, and driving measurable improvements in rural population health and provider sustainability.

data.title: TX - 2025 - Rural Texas Strong (rural-txstrong-prjct-narr)
data.highlights: Rural Texas Strong is a comprehensive strategy designed to reach 100% of Texas’s rural counties and invest in local wellness, prevention, and innovative solutions. The plan targets chronic illness, access to care, workforce recruitment, infrastructure, and technology modernization, including AI and telehealth. It prioritizes direct, local investments and is structured to align with CMS Rural Health Transformation Program goals.

data.title: TX - 2026 - Questions or feedback? Submit our Form.
data.highlights:
Texas will receive about $281.3 million annually during fiscal years 2026-2030. The program includes six major initiatives focused on improving rural health through infrastructure, AI and telehealth, patient empowerment, and workforce development. The Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) administers the program under the name Rural Texas Strong. Key contacts: RuralTexasStrong@hhsc.state.tx.us

data.title: SD - 2026 - Medicaid Primary Accountable Care Transformation (PACT) Initiative
data.highlights: South Dakota's PACT initiative establishes a new Medicaid primary care payment and quality incentive model, with $62.7M in grant funding for infrastructure, care management, and technology. The program aims to sustain rural primary care practices by shifting to value-based prospective payments, focusing on prevention, population health, and provider team support. Implementation runs from 2026-2030, beginning with planning and launching statewide in 2028.

keyDates.label: Medicaid case management/social work workshop launch

data.title: SD - 2026 - Strengthening Chronic Disease Management
data.highlights: This initiative focuses on expanding evidence-based chronic disease management programs in rural South Dakota, including funding for rural healthcare providers and caregiver support. It aims to improve health outcomes through sustainable community-based interventions and enhanced care coordination.

data.title: SD - 2026 - Integrated Behavioral Health System via CCBHC Certification and Collaborative Care Expansion
data.highlights: This initiative funds statewide implementation of CCBHC and Collaborative Care Models in South Dakota to improve behavioral health care in rural and frontier areas. It includes workforce development, crisis and telehealth infrastructure, payment system transformation, and data infrastructure modernization.

data.title: SD - 2025 - Regional Maternal and Infant Health Hubs
data.highlights: South Dakota will establish regional maternal and infant health hubs to strengthen clinical and social care coordination in rural and tribal areas. The initiative addresses workforce and social determinants barriers with support for doula programs and patient navigation.

data.title: SD - 2026 - South Dakota EMS System Enhancement
data.highlights: South Dakota's EMS initiative targets the development of EMS Hubs to improve coverage and response times, expands workforce training, and integrates advanced technology including telemedicine. The program aims to enhance rural emergency response sustainability and coordination statewide.

data.title: SD - 2026 - Rural Health Forward: Training and Resource Hub
data.highlights: The initiative will establish a statewide digital training platform and deliver virtual and in-person training to enhance rural healthcare workforce capabilities. It aims to improve care quality and provider retention through professional development.

data.title: SD - 2026 - Expand and Strengthen Rural Community Health Worker Workforce

keyDates.label: The Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) was established through H.R.1, the federal budget reconciliation bill signed into law on , 2025. In addition to introducing long-term changes to Medicaid and SNAP funding, H.R.1 created this five-year program to support rural health system transformation across the United States.

The program is administered by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and will provide funding to selected states from Federal Fiscal Year 2026 through 2030. All 50 states were eligible to apply. To be considered for funding, states were required to submit a comprehensive application, aligning with the Federal Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) by , 2025.

It outlines four primary initiative options: Health Outcomes Accelerator, Health System Flex Fund, Workforce Recruitment and Access, and Innovation & Technology Fund. The application requires detailed narrative, a continuity plan, data collection methods, and acknowledgment of federal and state compliance requirements.

data.title: NV - 2025 - Nevada RHTP / Rural Tribal Health Transformation
data.highlights: This RFA is Nevada’s formal invitation for Tribal Nations to apply for $8.1M in CMS Rural Health Transformation Program funds, targeting rural Tribal health infrastructure, innovation, and workforce. The program is specifically focused on supporting community-led, sustainable projects that complement Nevada’s wider Rural Health Transformation Plan. Awards and subrecipients have not yet been determined; all funding will be competitively awarded after May 29, 2026.

data.title: NV - 2024 - CMS RHT Grant Program
data.highlights: This guidance outlines the structure and requirements for applicants seeking RHTP funding to expand rural health specialty and subspecialty provider capacity in Nevada through workforce apprenticeship and training programs. Applicants must demonstrate local workforce needs and impacts, partner with rural providers and organizations, and provide a sustainability plan post-funding. Letters of commitment are required for non-rural and out-of-state applicants.

data.title: NV - 2026 - Nevada RHT Program (d2fac9)
data.highlights: This budget narrative template instructs applicants on how to request and justify funding under Nevada's RHT Program. The template outlines budget categories, administrative limits, and documentation requirements tied to RHT and CMS NOFO guidance. No sub-awards or recipient awards are specified in this guidance document.

data.title: NV - 2024 - CMS RHT Grant Opportunity
data.highlights: This guidance document outlines required project narrative and work plan elements for applicants seeking RHTP workforce funding in Nevada. Applicants must describe needs, work plans, recruitment/retention impact, partnerships, evaluation strategies, and sustainability beyond grant funding. Strong requirements for rural provider recruitment and a five-year service commitment are emphasized.

data.title: NV - 2026 - RHT Program Application - Nevada
data.highlights: This budget narrative template is customized for use in Nevada's RHT application. It describes proposed new staff positions to support program objectives, travel for rural workforce training, and acquisition of necessary equipment. Example personnel, operating, and travel costs are given, but all serve as illustrative placeholders.

data.title: NV - 2026 - RHT Program - Nevada
data.highlights: This document is a budget/application template for Nevada's involvement in the Rural Health Transformation Program, including example justifications for staff, travel, and equipment. Activities described include the hiring of new project staff, travel for remote patient monitoring training, and program supply purchases. Template references the CMS RHT NOFO and Nevada's application, confirming direct RHTP relevance.

data.title: NV - 2026 - Nevada RHTP (32cf8e)
data.highlights: This template provides detailed instructions on allowable costs, budget justification requirements, and category definitions for RHTP funding applicants in Nevada. It emphasizes compliance with both federal regulations (2 CFR 200) and state restrictions, including a cap on administrative expenses and a prohibition on indirect costs.

data.title: NV - 2026 - Nevada RHTP (wrrap_recruitment-and-retention-rfa-budget-narrative)
data.highlights: This template provides detailed instructions for applicants to the Nevada Rural Health Transformation Program on how to construct their budget narratives in compliance with program and federal requirements. It specifies allowable costs, administrative limitations, and required justifications for each budget category. The guidance emphasizes alignment between expenditures and program objectives and compliance with regulations for subrecipients and contractors.

data.title: NV - 2026 - Nevada Workforce Recruitment & Rural Access Program (WRRAP) – Provider Recruitment and Retention Program
data.highlights: This is a Request for Applications for Nevada's RHTP Workforce Recruitment & Rural Access Program (WRRAP) focused on supporting rural provider recruitment and retention for primary and preventive health care in rural Nevada. $32M is available for BP1, with no cost sharing required and a competitive tiered award approach. Targeted priorities include rural workforce gaps in hospitals, clinics, provider training, rural recruitment, and specialty service lines.

data.title: NV - 2026 - Nevada RHTP (final-attachment-c-rht-request-for-applications-flex-funds_budget_plan_template)
data.highlights: The application proposes hiring new positions, including a Project Director and Community Health Representatives (CHR), focused on implementing remote monitoring and quality improvement for rural health settings. Justifications link training, travel, and supply requests directly to CMS RHT NOFO and Nevada's RHT application objectives. Operating expenses include laptops, educational pamphlets, and software to facilitate program activities and reporting.

data.title: NV - 2025 - Nevada Rural Health System Flex Fund
data.highlights: The Nevada Rural Health System Flex Fund project will deploy telehealth infrastructure, staff training, and care coordination at rural clinic sites to expand access to primary care and behavioral health services for at least 300 rural residents. The program seeks to reduce avoidable emergency department use among high-risk patients and develop workforce capacity for sustainable telehealth delivery. Activities are coordinated with local clinics, hospitals, and a telehealth technology partner to maximize existing healthcare resources and enhance care continuity.

data.title: NV - 2026 - Nevada Rural Health System Flex Fund
data.highlights: This application details a project to expand telehealth-enabled care coordination for rural Nevada, focusing on two clinic sites and partnerships with regional hospitals and clinics. The initiative aims to serve at least 300 rural patients, reduce emergency department visits, and train 15 staff in telehealth. Technology, workforce, and care coordination improvements are central, with sustained operation planned beyond grant funding.

data.title: NV - 2026 - Nevada Rural Health System Flex Fund (511917)
data.highlights: This document is the narrative and guidance for applicants for the Nevada Rural Health System Flex Fund under the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). Applicants are required to describe the rural health challenge, current related efforts, goals, objectives using SMART format, and data collection/reporting plans. It includes instructions for letters of commitment and sustainability planning, but contains no actual awards or funding data.

data.title: NV - 2026 - RHT Grant Program
data.highlights: This is an application cover sheet form for the Nevada Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Grant Program to request funding and demonstrate eligibility as a subrecipient serving rural populations. data.title: NV - 2026 - Nevada RHT Program

An estimated $179.9 million federal award supports health system transformation in all rural Nevada counties.

No awards or funding commitments are stated; this is a pre-application guidance request to collect initiative ideas for the state plan.

data.title: ND - 2025 - North Dakota RHT Plan Project Narrative
data.highlights:
North Dakota's Rural Health Transformation Plan targets nearly half of the state's population living in rural and frontier areas, including significant American Indian communities. The plan identifies acute workforce shortages, high rates of chronic disease (especially among tribal and rural populations), and extensive access barriers for primary, specialty, behavioral, and emergency care. Major strategies include building workforce pipelines, modernizing telehealth infrastructure, right-sizing rural hospitals, investing in care coordination and technology, and advancing value-based payment models to stabilize provider finances. Innovative approaches span mobile clinics, community-based telehealth hubs, and targeted grants to address local wellness, behavioral health, and EMS needs. Key contacts: Sarah Aker; Krista Fremming; Lonny Mertz; Dirk Wilke
