data.title: MS - 2022 - Mississippi Division of Medicaid Medicaid Transformation
data.highlights: Mississippi Medicaid has implemented major payment and quality programs including hospital and physician access initiatives, ambulance reimbursement reforms, and health information exchange requirements. The state is executing a multi-year, data-driven quality strategy focusing on value-based care, improved population health, and robust stakeholder engagement. New technology systems and provider quality incentives are central to the transformation program.

data.title: ME - 2025 - MaineCare and Medicaid State Transformation under H.R.1
data.highlights: Sweeping federal Medicaid and SNAP reforms will substantially reduce coverage for rural, low-income, and immigrant Mainers while shifting financial risk to the state, rural hospitals, and safety-net providers. Rural counties see the highest Medicaid reliance and will be most impacted by work requirements, payment and tax changes, and loss of family planning and SNAP education funding. Maine faces a potential $5 billion Medicaid/SNAP reduction over 10 years.

data.title: MS - 2023 - Mississippi Medicaid Transformation and Hospital Access/Quality Programs
data.highlights: The Mississippi Division of Medicaid is transforming rural health and hospital payment structures through initiatives such as the Mississippi Hospital Access Program (MHAP) and directed quality incentive arrangements, linking payments to preventable readmission and complications metrics and participation in statewide health information networks. The TREAT program provides enhanced EMS reimbursement using a provider tax, and maternal health is prioritized through extended postpartum coverage and app-based resources. Substantial technology upgrades to MMIS and process improvements are underway to support system integration and further Medicaid modernization.

data.title: MS - 2025 - Mississippi RHTP
data.highlights: Mississippi Medicaid is collaborating with MSDH and the Governor's Office on a Rural Health Transformation Program application. Multiple Medicaid initiatives are being implemented, including new value-based payment incentives and maternal health transformation grants. The MHAP and QIPP programs continue to drive hospital performance and access improvements.

data.title: MS - 2024 - Mississippi Outcomes for Maternal Safety (MOMS) Initiative - Value-Based Payment Incentive Program
data.highlights: The Mississippi Division of Medicaid's MOMS Initiative is launching a maternal health incentive program under the Value-Based Payment framework, focusing on severe maternal morbidity risk assessment, improved postpartum care coordination, and incentivized timely follow-up. Key partners include Medicaid, multiple CCOs, and hospital providers, with technology investments in HIE connectivity anticipated by December 2024. MS leads the nation in maternal morbidity, and this program aims to address both medical and social determinants of health through structured risk-based care pathways.

data.title: MS - 2025 - MOMS Program - Mississippi Division of Medicaid
data.highlights: The Mississippi MOMS Initiative introduces a Risk Screening Tool to ensure targeted postpartum care for Medicaid beneficiaries beginning January 2025. Special emphasis is placed on early, risk-stratified postpartum visits, with in-person assessments required for the highest-risk patients. The policy aims to reduce historically high rates of maternal mortality, especially among Black women, and addresses both rural access issues and health system coordination.

data.title: MS - 2024 - Mississippi Division of Medicaid Value-Based Payment (VBP) Incentive Program – MOMS Initiative
data.highlights: The Mississippi Division of Medicaid is implementing the Value-Based Payment (VBP) Incentive Program with a major focus on improving maternal health outcomes through the MOMS Initiative. The program incentivizes hospitals and outpatient providers for timely risk assessment and postpartum follow-up of maternal beneficiaries. Implementation involves care management, health information exchange, and coordinated case management across providers and CCOs.

data.title: MS - 2025 - Mississippi Outcomes for Maternal Safety (MOMS) Initiative
data.highlights: The Mississippi Outcomes for Maternal Safety (MOMS) initiative is part of MSDOM's Value-Based Payment Incentive Program to address rising Severe Maternal Morbidity (SMM). The program establishes a standardized risk assessment for all maternal discharges, with linked incentives for timely postpartum follow-up and care management. The guidance directs hospitals to implement these assessments and ensure care transitions to outpatient providers.

data.title: MS - 2022 - Mississippi Medicaid Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP)
data.highlights: Mississippi’s Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP) ties a large proportion of hospital Medicaid payments to measurable quality improvement metrics, particularly focusing on potentially preventable complications (PPCs) and hospital returns (PPHR/PPED). COVID-19's impact on hospital use prompted changes in measurement periods and analytical approach. Hospitals must certify receipt of reports, and are required to implement corrective action plans and reach performance thresholds to receive full incentive funding.

data.title: MS - 2018 - Mississippi Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP) for Rural Hospitals
data.highlights: This supplement details Mississippi's QIPP payment methodology, focusing on reducing potentially preventable hospital returns (PPHRs) in Medicaid populations. Payments and incentives are tied to hospitals meeting quality performance targets, with corrective action plans required for underperforming hospitals. COVID-19 impacts are accounted for in cycle 3 through a change in the baseline period.

data.title: MS - 2022 - Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP) – Potentially Preventable Hospital Return (PPHR), Potentially Preventable Complications (PPC), Health Information Network (HIN)
data.highlights: This document sets operational timelines for the Mississippi Division of Medicaid’s QIPP program related to rural hospitals. It covers attestation processes, payment schedules, and corrective action planning for hospitals based on measured readmissions, complications, and health information network participation. The program provides quality-linked payments as part of rural Medicaid transformation efforts.

data.title: MS - 2023 - Mississippi Medicaid Health Information Network (HIN) Attestation
data.highlights: This attestation form documents hospitals' participation and connection to the statewide Health Information Network (HIN) required for Medicaid program compliance. The HIN supports clinical and ADT data exchange to improve care delivery for Mississippi Medicaid beneficiaries, including those served by rural hospitals. No specific RHTP or HIN funding amounts or individual hospital sub-awards are stated in this document.

data.title: MS - 2023 - Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP) (QIPP-Schedule-SFY-2023-Revised-1)
data.highlights: This document provides detailed quarterly guidance for hospitals participating in the Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP) in Mississippi for SFY 2023. It outlines required timelines for attestation submission, reporting on potentially preventable returns and complications, and associated notifications between Medicaid, hospitals, and teams. Focus is placed on routine performance monitoring and active hospital engagement to improve rural health outcomes.

data.title: MS - 2023 - Mississippi Medicaid Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP)
data.highlights: Mississippi's Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP) links the majority of its Medicaid hospital payments to quality and outcomes, with rigorous performance targets for readmissions and preventable complications. Hospitals are required to regularly report, attest, and implement corrective action plans, with payments at risk for non-performance. Care management, health information technology, and population health strategies are central to driving improvement across both physical and behavioral health domains.

data.title: MS - 2023 - Mississippi Hospital PPC Corrective Action Plan
data.highlights: This report outlines corrective action planning requirements for Mississippi hospitals to reduce rates of Potentially Preventable Complications (PPCs) in Medicaid. Hospitals are expected to set S.M.A.R.T. goals and milestones, detail actions, analyze root causes, and implement policy changes as part of the quality improvement cycle. Performance is assessed over a 2-year improvement period with results reviewed in 2026.

data.title: MS - 2023 - Mississippi Medicaid Hospital PPHR Corrective Action Plan
data.highlights: Mississippi hospitals participating in Medicaid are required to submit corrective action plans for reducing readmissions, with specific actions including staff education, patient awareness, and community partnerships. Hospitals must demonstrate at least a 2% improvement in their A/E ratio during the performance incentive period, and all Medicaid beneficiaries must be screened for mental health disorders on admission. The plan emphasizes measurable targets and reporting for rural health transformation.

data.title: MS - 2019 - Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP) - Potentially Preventable Complications (PPC)
data.highlights: This Methodology Supplement outlines the Mississippi QIPP PPC approach to incentivizing quality improvement in Medicaid inpatient care. Statewide PPC performance for fiscal years 2019–2020 showed a weighted actual-to-expected ratio of 1.10, prompting targeted corrective action plans for underperforming hospitals. Incentives and penalties are based on hospital attainment and improvement of PPC performance, with a focus on reducing costly complications such as septicemia.

data.title: MS - 2023 - Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP)
data.highlights: This document outlines the methodology and operational guidance for the Mississippi QIPP PPHR component, establishing casemix-adjusted statewide quality targets for hospital readmissions and return ED visits. Performance is measured using the 3M PPR/ED algorithm with explicit targets for corrective action plans and incentive payment adjustments. The program is structured in three-year cycles with annual determination of performance, corrective action, and payment based on hospitals’ actual-to-expected readmission ratios.

data.title: MS - 2024 - Mississippi Medicaid Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP)
data.highlights: Mississippi's Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP) links a significant portion of hospital Medicaid payments to performance on quality metrics, including potentially preventable complications (PPCs) and hospital returns (PPHRs). The program requires statewide hospital participation in health information exchange, and imposes corrective action plans, attestation requirements, and at-risk payments based on performance. Multiple managed care organizations and hospital systems are actively collaborating to reduce readmissions and improve outcomes.

data.title: MS - 2024 - Mississippi Division of Medicaid Health Information Network (HIN) Attestation
data.highlights: This attestation document verifies that various Mississippi hospitals have an active contract with the statewide Health Information Network (HIN) during SFY 2024. HIN participation supports Medicaid compliance for data sharing and reporting. No individual hospital awards or funding amounts are specified.

data.title: MS - 2024 - Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP)
data.highlights: This document provides the Mississippi Division of Medicaid QIPP operational calendar for SFY2024, including quarterly timelines and deadlines for Health Information Network (HIN) attestations and reporting of Potentially Preventable Hospital Return (PPHR) and Complications (PPC). It outlines communications and deadlines to ensure Medicaid hospitals participate in quality measurement activities. This process supports hospital engagement in quality improvement and health information technology as part of the Rural Health Transformation Program.

data.title: MS - 2024 - Mississippi Hospital PPC Corrective Action Plan
data.highlights: This Corrective Action Plan requires Mississippi rural hospitals to achieve a 2% reduction in their PPC A/E ratios over the upcoming performance period. Hospitals must list and analyze their top five Potentially Preventable Complications, institute S.M.A.R.T. goals, and implement staff education and policy/process changes, with oversight by the Division of Medicaid. Hospital performance will be assessed in 2027, and success will impact future incentives.

data.title: MS - 2024 - Mississippi Hospital PPHR Corrective Action Plan
data.highlights: This Mississippi Hospital PPHR Corrective Action Plan focuses on reducing readmissions among Medicaid beneficiaries by improving A/E ratios and implementing targeted actions. Key components include tracking top readmission causes, staff education, post-discharge patient follow-up, and comprehensive mental health screening on admission. The performance period runs through June 2025, with statewide programmatic reporting due January 2026.

data.title: MS - 2025 - Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP) (AMPPC-Training-Presentation_FINAL-1-23-2025)
data.highlights: Mississippi Medicaid's QIPP transitions a substantial share of payments to hospitals from volume- to quality-linked, incentivizing improved outcomes for rural and urban hospitals. The 2025 structure adds new ambulatory preventable complication tracking, leveraging proprietary Solventum tools for data analysis and reporting. Hospitals must regularly attest to report receipt, with financial penalties tied to participation and outcomes.

data.title: MS - 2025 - Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP)
data.highlights: The Mississippi Division of Medicaid is implementing its 2025 Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP), with structured quarterly timelines for attestation, reporting, and corrective action. The program includes Health Information Network reporting and tracking of potential hospital complications, targeting improvement in rural hospitals. Deadlines and notification processes are clearly delineated, partnering with external support and hospitals statewide.

data.title: MS - 2025 - Mississippi Hospital PPC Corrective Action Plan
data.highlights: This document outlines Mississippi's hospital-level approach to reducing Potentially Preventable Complications as part of a Medicaid Quality Improvement initiative aligned with RHTP requirements. Hospitals are required to set S.M.A.R.T. goals, conduct root cause analyses, and document education/policy efforts related to PPCs. There are defined assessment periods and measurable targets for performance improvement tied to rural health transformation.

data.title: MS - 2025 - Mississippi Hospital PPHR Corrective Action Plan (CAP)
data.highlights: This required CAP document is part of Mississippi's hospital Medicaid transformation to reduce readmissions and improve quality. It includes a focus on staff and patient education, community partnerships, S.M.A.R.T. goal setting, and mandatory mental health screening for Medicaid patients at admission. It aligns with payment incentive periods and quality benchmarks under the RHTP.

data.title: MS - 2026 - Mississippi Division of Medicaid Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP)
data.highlights: Mississippi QIPP will direct $50 million for value-based payments to hospitals, incentivizing quality and outcome improvements for Medicaid beneficiaries—including rural facilities. Payments are tied to performance in reducing potentially preventable hospital returns (PPHR), inpatient complications (PPC), and ambulatory complications (AM-PPC), with rigorous reporting and corrective action plan requirements. Notable emphasis on maternal health with the new MOMS initiative launching in SFY 2026.

data.title: MS - 2026 - Mississippi Hospital Access Program (MHAP)
data.highlights: The Mississippi Hospital Access Program (MHAP) establishes a payment and quality incentive framework for Medicaid managed care hospitals, including monthly and quarterly payments based on fee schedule adjustments and quality metrics. MHAP incorporates a Quality Incentive Payment Program (QIPP) focusing on hospital readmissions and complications, with corrective action and performance improvement cycles. The program prepares for alignment with new CMS managed care finance rules starting in state fiscal year 2029.

data.title: MS - 2022 - Mississippi Division of Medicaid Managed Care EQR Validation of Encounter Data (CAN and CHIP)
data.highlights: This report details an External Quality Review (EQR) of CY 2022 Medicaid and CHIP encounter data submitted by UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Mississippi. While encounter data completeness met required state and federal thresholds, accuracy rates were consistently below the 98% benchmark. Recommendations are provided to improve the integrity and timeliness of managed care encounter submissions in Mississippi.

data.title: MS - 2025 - Mississippi Medicaid Comprehensive Quality Strategy
data.highlights: Mississippi Division of Medicaid's updated Comprehensive Quality Strategy (CQS) guides quality improvement efforts in Medicaid managed care and fee-for-service. Central priorities include maternal health, chronic disease, behavioral and child/adolescent health, and advancing value-based payment. External Quality Review ensures accountability while new value-based initiatives incentivize measurable improvements.

data.title: US - 2026 - Federal RHTP Summary 2026-2030
data.highlights: This document summarizes the $50 billion federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP) established by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in July 2025. It outlines RHTP program structure, state application requirements for transformation plans, allowable uses of funds—including quality improvement, technology adoption, workforce recruitment, and financial stabilization—and program milestones. The summary details the definition of eligible rural health facilities and requirements for annual reporting and compliance.

data.title: MO - 2026 - Invitation to Comment: RHTP
data.highlights: The Missouri Department of Social Services is soliciting public input to shape Missouri's application for the new Rural Health Transformation Program, a federal initiative distributing $50 billion nationwide between 2026 and 2030. Missouri has not yet received a funding award amount, as the application process is pending CMS guidance.

data.title: MO - 2026 - rural health
data.highlights:
The program includes a $40 million multi-phase funding strategy emphasizing the ToRCH Care model with priority service lines in maternal health, behavioral health, and diagnostics/outpatient care. Key initiatives include expanding mobile integrated healthcare, community paramedicine, and rural maternal health workforce development. The program selected 27 Hub Anchor organizations across the state to lead regional implementation and foster collaboration.

data.highlights: The Mississippi Division of Medicaid has developed a statewide quality strategy for 2026-2029 focused on care improvement, value-based payment, and rural health transformation. Strategies include new incentive programs for hospitals and MCOs, targeted initiatives in maternal and chronic disease, programs supporting rural hospitals, and efforts to address longstanding health disparities and provider shortages. The program governs over 700,000 Medicaid and CHIP enrollees, with substantial rural population coverage.

data.title: MS - 2018 - Mississippi Division of Medicaid Rural Health and Hospital Transformation Policy Updates
data.highlights: This summary covers multiple years of Mississippi Medicaid legislative updates affecting rural hospitals and Medicaid populations, including alternative outpatient payment options for rural hospitals, expanded Medicaid coverage for women, and pilot programs to monitor hospital and system capacity. No explicit RHTP transformation awards or recent direct CMS-to-hospital grants were found. Document is a state-level policy/legislation summary, not an award list.

data.title: MS - 2024 - Comprehensive Quality Strategy and Value-Based Incentive Programs 2024-2025
data.highlights:
Mississippi’s Medicaid program has expanded value-based care through comprehensive payment and quality incentive programs for rural hospitals, physicians, and emergency providers. Programs like MHAP, QIPP, MAPS, TREAT, and MOMS are designed to improve access, care quality, and outcomes statewide. Recent additions include new maternal health and quality metrics, as well as increased investments for rural hospital stability. Key contacts: QIPP@medicaid.ms.gov; TREAT@medicaid.ms.gov

data.highlights: Minnesota is soliciting public input to inform the state’s Rural Health Transformation Program, seeking ideas to sustainably improve rural health care delivery. Focus areas include emergency, primary, chronic, mental, and maternal health, as well as workforce and technology solutions. The document provides structured prompts for input on evidence-based interventions, innovative care models, workforce development, and technology use.

data.title: MN - 2025 - Minnesota RHTP
data.highlights: This FAQ provides guidance on Minnesota’s Rural Health Transformation Program proposal, outlining five major initiatives submitted to CMS, covering preventive care, workforce recruitment, access, regional care models, and technology. Details on funding opportunities, program structure, and grant procedures are pending final federal award and will be released by MDH. Organizational eligibility, allowable expenses, reporting, and administrative caps are discussed in preparation for forthcoming grant activities.

data.title: MN - 2025 - RHT Application Project Narrative
data.highlights:
Minnesota's RHTP application offers a statewide, multi-pronged approach combining workforce expansion, technology adoption, provider collaboration, and targeted improvements in chronic disease, maternal, and behavioral health outcomes. The plan focuses on collaborative learning, local flexibility, scalable innovations, and direct investment in rural and Tribal settings, aiming to improve health outcomes, retention, and sustainability of rural services in all regions of rural Minnesota.

data.title: MD - 2025 - Maryland Rural Health Strategic Plan
data.highlights: The Maryland Rural Health Strategic Plan outlines three key priorities to enhance rural health: engaging communities, leveraging health in all policies, and building a coordinated health system integrating public health and clinical care. It provides a data-driven overview and actionable objectives for 2025-2030.

data.title: MD - 2026 - Maryland RHTP (MD-RHTP-FAQ-Public-Facing)
data.highlights: Maryland received a $168 million CMS cooperative award for Rural Health Transformation in 2026. RHTP focuses on workforce, sustainable access/innovation, and nutrition for health across 18 rural counties. Competitive funding opportunities and implementation details will roll out April–August 2026.

data.title: MD - 2024 - Maryland RHTP
data.highlights: This Maryland-focused Rural Health Vendor Directory connects rural health program stakeholders to a diverse set of vendors and service providers relevant to the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). It catalogs offerings for workforce, HIT, telemedicine, care navigation, community health initiatives, and technology adoption to inform strategic engagement and project planning. No funding, awards, or recipient grants are documented; the directory is strictly for informational and networking purposes.

data.title: MD - 2026 - Maryland RHTP (MD-RHTP-Pillar-2-Transformation-RFA)
data.highlights: Maryland RHTP plans to distribute $134.8 million in subawards through competitive processes focusing on transformational projects in rural health. The State intends to combine three Pillar 2 transformation funds into one unified RFA expected in late April 2026.

data.title: MD - 2025 - Maryland RHTP Plan
data.highlights:
Maryland's Rural Health Transformation Program Plan outlines a strategy to use RHTP funds to target workforce development, transform care access points, expand primary and specialty care, behavioral health, and address chronic disease. Maryland plans to implement three main initiatives with an estimated $992 million budget over five years. The strategy employs both immediate impact and transformation subgrant funding, aiming to reach all 18 state-designated rural counties and improve rural health outcomes through value-based care, partnerships, and data-driven solutions. Key contacts: Sara Seitz; Elizabeth Edsall Kromm, Ph.D., M.Sc.

It describes the distribution mechanism, allowable activities, and strategic goals of RHTP, designed to stabilize and strengthen rural hospitals, support workforce, and promote technology-driven solutions for rural communities.

The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) engaged rural health providers, community partners, and Medicaid beneficiaries to develop a strategy guiding the use of RHT Program funds to support rural providers' sustainability and growth amid anticipated federal funding cuts. The program includes transparent reporting of subrecipients and is governed by an advisory council. Key contacts: MDHHS-RHTP@michigan.gov

data.highlights: This document summarizes Maine's anticipated participation in the new $50B Rural Health Transformation Program. Maine expects to apply for and receive approximately $500M over five years, pending application approval. The plan emphasizes expeditious deployment of funds through innovation, infrastructure, workforce, technology, and robust public engagement, to offset significant new losses from federal Medicaid cuts.

data.title: ME - 2026 - Maine RHTP
data.highlights: Maine was awarded approximately $190M for its Year 1 RHTP transformation, as part of a new federal rural health program established by H.R. 1 and managed by CMS. Maine will implement five major initiatives addressing population health, workforce, technology, care access, and financial sustainability, with an emphasis on rapid contracting and community engagement. Contracts and subawards will be competitively bid, with key activities focused on expanding mobile health, telehealth, care delivery innovations, hospital and workforce sustainability, and mental health services.

data.title: ME - 2025 - Maine RHTP (V2_SoM_RHTP_Project_Narrative_11Dec25_CMS_Response_ADDED)
data.highlights: Maine’s RHTP strategy uses five pillars: population health, workforce, technology innovation, affordability and access, and financial sustainability for rural providers. The plan targets over 690,000 rural residents facing poor health status, provider shortages, and financial instability. Strategic initiatives include expanding telehealth, behavioral and maternal health, workforce pipelines, system-level financial supports, and cross-sector partnerships to bridge access, care quality, and sustainability gaps.

data.title: ME - 2025 - MaineCare (Medicaid), RHTP Impact
data.highlights: The federal budget law effective July 2025 will dramatically reshape Medicaid (MaineCare), SNAP, and Marketplace coverage for rural and low-income Mainers, introducing stricter eligibility and financial provisions as well as significant state costs. Rural hospitals face direct threats to stable Medicaid funding; eligibility, administrative, and provider tax changes risk $5 billion in MaineCare costs over 10 years, with major coverage losses possible. Maine DHHS is pursuing stakeholder engagement, education, and federal advocacy to mitigate harm.

The program spans a five-year period starting from 2026, with efforts to improve care delivery and health outcomes in rural communities across Maine.

Selected vendors will review, advise, and help monitor HIT investments by rural hospitals, clinics, FQHCs, tribal organizations, and related subgrantees, with an anticipated 150 provider organizations applying annually. The contract supports technical review, conflict-of-interest monitoring, and strategic guidance to MN Department of Health for effective rural HIT adoption. Key contacts: Ann Linde rural.transformation.mdh@state.mn.us; Katie Burns rural.transformation.mdh@state.mn.us

- Anticipated Contract Term - 05/15/2026 – 04/30/2028 - CT

data.title: MN - 2026 - RHTP Funding - MN Dept. of Health
data.highlights: The program provides multiple funding opportunities focused on workforce retention, child and adolescent mental health, tele-buprenorphine access, technical assistance for health IT, telehealth access points, and Project ECHO for maternal and behavioral health. These initiatives aim to improve rural healthcare access and capacity across Minnesota's rural communities. Key contacts: health.orhpc@state.mn.us

data.title: CA - 2026 - California RHT (CalRHT) Program Briefing (California-Rural-Health-Transformation-Program-Briefing-March-2026)
data.highlights:
California was awarded $233.6M for Budget Period 1 of the CMS Rural Health Transformation Program. The CalRHT initiative aims to strengthen rural health care access, workforce, technology infrastructure, and care networks statewide. Key priorities include broad stakeholder input, workforce development, technology investments, and innovative models for maternal and primary care. Key contacts: CalRHT Program Team CalRHT@hcai.ca.gov

data.title: NV - 2026 - Nevada's RHT Program Initiatives (rhtp-initiatives)
data.highlights: Nevada’s RHT Program priorities were collaboratively developed with broad rural healthcare stakeholder involvement and the Governor’s Office. The program emphasizes avoiding fiscal cliffs and aims for sustainable improvements in rural healthcare access over the five-year grant period.

data.title: UT - 2025 - RHTP - Utah Department of Health and Human Services
data.highlights:
Utah was awarded $195 million in its first year from CMS to launch RHTP, receiving at least $100 million annually for FY2026-FY2030. The program is driven by four strategic goals and incorporates seven broad initiatives, targeting improved health outcomes, access, quality, strengthened workforce, and the modernization of rural healthcare infrastructure with extensive stakeholder engagement. Key contacts: ruralht@utah.gov

data.title: SD - 2026 - Building a Stronger, Healthier Rural South Dakota (rural-health-transformation-project)

The program secured approximately $189.4 million in federal funding to enhance rural health across the state, focusing on expanding telehealth, improving broadband, supporting rural workforce recruitment, and addressing transportation barriers. The Department of Health awarded grants including $90 million for digital health modernization and $31.5 million for Rural Strong grants to improve care access and quality. data.title: SD - 2026 - State of South Dakota Announces Second Round of RHT Requests for Proposals
data.highlights:
The program focuses on improving access to care, digital health modernization, and long-term sustainability for rural communities. New initiatives include workforce advancement for doulas, statewide maternal health assessments, and development of Rural Health Forward—a resource hub to bridge educational gaps between urban and rural healthcare professionals. Strategic investments and cross-agency collaborations drive a resilient, connected healthcare system across South Dakota. Key contacts: Tia Kafka DOHMedia@state.sd.us; Melissa Magstadt

data.title: DE - 2025 - Delaware RHTP Executive Budget Summary (Final-RHTP-Revised-Budget-1.30.26)
data.highlights:
The Delaware Rural Health Transformation strategy unites 15 initiatives to expand access, strengthen the workforce, modernize technology, and improve population health in rural Sussex and Kent Counties. Over $786 million is budgeted, with direct investments in clinical infrastructure, technology, and new models like Rural Hope Centers. The plan features robust performance tracking, stakeholder partnerships, and an emphasis on sustainable capacity building. Key contacts: Katherine Hughes; Chelsea Kammermeier; Christopher Masten; Lakeesha Johns
